THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 6, 1932
S. B. REGISTER
3380.
6.19.32

Work Done, Lord Lytton
And Party Quit Shores
Of China For Trip Home

Triestino Liner Gange Also Carries Dr. Koo To
Geneva; Heavy Guard At Jetty; Date Of
Report Publication Unknown

TEXT OF SURVEY GUARDED—"YOUR LAST
CHANCE" LYTTON TELLS SCRIBES

Lord Lytton, "father" of the League of Nations Commission report bearing his name, sailed from Shanghai at 11.30 a.m. yesterday for Geneva, via Milan, on the Lloyd Triestino liner Gange with the American and Italian members of his party and Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo, Chinese assessor to the League, also en route to Europe there to assume the twin posts of Chinese delegate to the League council meeting and Minister to France. To the last Lord Lytton, British member and chairman of the Commission, kept his secret well, that concerning the contents of the lengthy report on Sino-Japanese conditions in Manchuria which the entire world is awaiting tensely. "This is your last chance," he told reporters affably as he was taken on the steamer's gangplank by cameramen.

Extreme vigilance was shown by the various local policing bodies who mustered more than 150 men at the Customs jetty by 8.30 a.m. These maintained a cordon which separated the two parties, that of Lord Lytton and that of Dr. Koo, from a crowd of 200 persons that gathered to see the send-off.

Those accompanying the League head, members of the Commission formed in the hectic days of last January and which has been travelling over the actual trouble grounds in the Far East since last March, were General F. R. McCoy, American member, and Count Aldrovandi Mare-Scotti, Italian member. Others in the party included Mrs. McCoy and the Hon. W. W. Astor. Dr. E. Scunce and General Claudel, the German and French members of the Commission, are returning to Geneva via Harbin and Siberia.

Date Of Report

Mystery meanwhile surrounds the date on which the sensational report is to be published. It was signed unanimously on Saturday morning at Peiping, a voluminous document purported to contain more than 100,000 words. Two sealed copies are being left behind, one for China, the other for Japan. On an as yet unnamed date it will be published simultaneously throughout the world. That this may occur before the two parties reach Geneva is indicated in rumours to the effect that the report will go part of the way by aeroplane. The League will not consider it, it is believed, at the forthcoming League Assembly but at a special session early in November.

Dr. Koo's party was first at the jetty yesterday. He had received at his home, at 9.30, Mr. T. V. Soong, acting President of the Executive Yuan and Minister of Finance; Mr. Wang Ching-wei, ex-President of the Yuan, and Dr. Lo Wen-kan, Minister of Foreign Affairs. With these dignitaries and six secretaries who are taking the trip with him, he boarded the Customs launch Ching Hui at 9.46.

Band Plays

Lord Lytton arrived a minute later, accompanied by his party and Mayor Wu Teh-chen of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai. He stepped upon The Bund from his motor car and shook hands with Sir Frederick Maze, Inspector-General of Customs; Sir John F. Brenan, K.C.M.G., British Consul-General; Count C. di Ciano, Italian Minister, and many other foreign and Chinese leading personages. The band of the Municipality's police force was meanwhile playing. More than 100 International Settlement police, headed by Superintendent I. Robertson, 40 police belonging to the Bureau of Public Safety and a group of Customs officers were present to keep the cordon effective.

Lord Lytton and his party boarded the Bureau's steam launch "Kung An" and arrived at the steamer's side at 10.02 a.m. As he walked up the gangplank he stopped for a moment, seeing that the photographers were eager for some last "shots" and called to them that it was their last chance.

When Mrs. McCoy arrived at the door of the liner's music room she was presented with a bouquet by Miss Liu, daughter of Mrs. Liu Dsang-shi, Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs. Several other bouquets followed.

Captain Camelli of the Gange asked members of the two parties in to the dining saloon to rest. There they joined in a toast in champagne.

The visitors left the ship at 10.25. It had been planned to sail at 11 but an adverse tide delayed the start half an hour. In a few last words to the press Dr. Koo made a final plea to Chinese to work hard together for the country's salvation.

To Land In Venice

Lord Lytton's personal plans are to land in Venice from the Gange, where he will be met probably by his daughter, Lady Hermanie Cobbold, who lives in Milan. After a visit with her he will proceed to England and, it is believed, be met there by his wife.

The two Commission members taking the land route intend to leave Harbin on September 12. They may fly, with the remaining members of the staff and the Secretariat, from Harbin to either Tsitsihar or Manchuli, if conditions require it.

The work of Lord Lytton has received high commendation from various circles because of the unfaltering way he carried on despite a serious and lengthy illness. That he should have come through in such a fashion in the face of so arduous and delicate a task as he and his Commission were called upon to perform, has won for him much praise. His unfailing courtesy, tact and patience, it is believed and hoped, will have contributed much to the solution of the delicate situation in the Far East.

JBR 6/9.

1932年6月19日

李顿勋爵完成工作
及其一行离开中国海岸
启程回国

意大利特里奥斯蒂诺轮船公司“恒河号”班轮亦载顾博士前往
日内瓦；码头戒备森严；报告发布日期未定

调查报告内容保密——李顿对记者称“这是你们最后的机会”

以其名字命名的国际联盟委员会报告之“父”李顿勋爵，于昨日上午11时30分从上海启程，经米兰前往日内瓦，乘坐的是意大利特里奥斯蒂诺轮船公司（Lloyd Triestino）的“恒河号”（Gange）班轮。同行的有该团的美国和意大利成员，以及国联中方顾问顾维钧（V. K. Wellington Koo）博士，顾博士亦正前往欧洲，将在当地就任国联理事会会议中国代表及驻法国公使的双重职务。直到最后一刻，身为英国成员兼委员会主席的李顿勋爵仍严守秘密，即关于全世界紧张等待的、有关满洲中日局势的长篇报告的内容。“这是你们最后的机会，”当摄影师簇拥着他走上船舷跳板时，他和蔼地对记者们说道。

各地方警务机构表现出极高的警惕性，至上午8时30分已在海关码头集结了150多名人员。他们维持着一道警戒线，将李顿勋爵一行和顾博士一行与聚集观看送行的200名人群隔离开来。

陪同这位国联负责人、即在今年1月那段动荡日子里组建并自今年3月以来一直在远东实际冲突地区巡视的委员会成员的，有美国成员麦考伊（F. R. McCoy）将军和意大利成员阿尔德罗万迪·马雷-斯科蒂（Aldrovandi Mare-Scotti）伯爵。随行人员中还包括麦考伊夫人和W. W. 阿斯特（W. W. Astor）阁下。委员会的德国和法国成员埃·斯昆斯（E. Scunce）博士和克劳德尔（Claudel）将军，正经由哈尔滨和西伯利亚返回日内瓦。

报告日期

与此同时，这份轰动性报告的发布日期仍是个谜。该报告已于周六上午在北平一致签署，这是一份据称包含超过10万字的大部头文件。两份密封副本被留下，一份给中国，另一份给日本。它将在一个尚未公布的日期向全世界同时发布。有传言称报告将部分通过航空运输，这表明在两派人员抵达日内瓦之前，报告可能就会发布。据信，国联不会在即将召开的国联大会上审议此报告，而是在11月初的一次特别会议上审议。

顾博士一行昨日最先抵达码头。他于9时30分在其寓所接待了行政院代院长兼财政部长宋子文先生、前行政院院长汪精卫先生以及外交部长罗文干博士。在这些显贵以及随他同行的六名秘书的陪同下，他于9时46分登上了海关小艇“静海号”（Ching Hui）。

乐队演奏

李顿勋爵随后于一分钟后抵达，由其随行人员及大上海特别市市长吴铁城陪同。他从汽车踏上外滩，并与海关税务司梅乐和（Frederick Maze）爵士、英国总领事布伦南（John F. Brenan）爵士（K.C.M.G.）、意大利公使齐亚诺（C. di Ciano）伯爵以及许多其他中外知名人士握手。此时，市局警队乐队正在演奏。一百多名公共租界警察，由督察长I. 罗伯逊（I. Robertson）率领，四十名隶属于公安局的警察以及一组海关官员在场，以维持警戒线的有效运作。

李顿勋爵及其一行登上公安局的蒸汽小艇“公安号”（Kung An），并于上午10时02分抵达轮船旁。当他走上跳板时，稍作停留，见摄影师急于拍摄最后的“镜头”，便向他们喊道，这是他们最后的机会。

当麦考伊夫人到达轮船音乐室门口时，外交部次长刘崇杰（Liu Dsang-shi，音译）夫人的女儿刘小姐向她献上了一束花。随后又献上了几束花。

“恒河号”船长卡梅利（Camelli）邀请两派人员进入餐厅休息。在那里，他们共同举杯香槟祝酒。

访客于10时25分离船。原计划于11时开船，但因逆潮延误了半小时。在对媒体说的最后几句话中，顾博士再次呼吁中国人共同努力，以拯救国家。

将在威尼斯登陆

李顿勋爵的个人计划是乘“恒河号”在威尼斯登陆，届时可能由居住在米兰的女儿赫尔曼妮·科博尔德（Hermanie Cobbold）女爵迎接。在探望她之后，他将前往英国，据信其妻子将在那里与他汇合。

取陆路的两名委员会成员打算于9月12日离开哈尔滨。如果情况需要，他们可能会与其余工作人员及秘书处成员一起，从哈尔滨飞往齐齐哈尔或满洲里。

李顿勋爵的工作受到了各界的高度赞扬，因为他在严重且长期的疾病困扰下，仍以坚定不移的方式开展工作。面对他和他的委员会被要求执行的如此艰巨而微妙的任务，他能以这种方式坚持下来，赢得了诸多赞誉。人们相信并希望，他那始终如一的礼貌、机智和耐心，将为解决远东的微妙局势做出巨大贡献。

JBR 9月6日。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 5, 1932

Lord Lytton And Party
Arrive At Shanghai By
Aeroplane From Peiping

Full Story Of Early Morning Signing Of The
Historic Document; Lord Lytton Says The
World Must Judge Of Finished Work

PARTY TO SAIL FOR EUROPE BY GANGE
LEAVING HERE THIS MORNING

Lord Lytton, head of the League of Nations Commission
of Inquiry into Manchuria, accompanied by General and Mrs.
McCoy, Count Aldrovandi and members of his suite, arrived
at Hungjao Aerodrome yesterday afternoon in Marshal
Chang Hsueh-liang's tri-motored Ford aeroplane after a
six-hour flight from Peiping for the purpose of boarding the
s.s. Gange which is to sail for Europe early this morning.
The report of the Commission had only been completed and
signed in Peiping early yesterday morning and the task of
the Commission has now ended. Lord Lytton declined to
grant any newspaper interviews yesterday afternoon and
after being officially welcomed here, went to the Cathay
Hotel from where he will embark this morning.

early at 1 o'clock the
aerodrome at Hungjao was being
well guarded by police of the
Public Safety Bureau under
General Wen Ying-shing, the
Commissioner. There were also
a number of Chinese soldiers on
guard and police officers from the
Shanghai Municipal Council.
By the time the giant air-liner
arrived at 3.50 p.m., having left
Peiping at 10 a.m., there were at
least 200 people at the aerodrome
to give the distinguished visitors
a welcome. Among those pre-
sent were noticed Mayor Wu Teh-
chen, Dr. Wellington V. K. Koo
(newly-appointed Chinese Min-
ister to France), Count C. di
Ciano (Italian Minister), Mr. Liu
Dzong-zih (Vice-Minister for
Foreign Affairs), representatives
of the Chinese General Chamber
of Commerce and many leading
foreign and Chinese personalities.
Hearty Welcome
A hearty welcome was accord-
ed Lord Lytton and the other
eight passengers of the plane,
Mayor Wu and Dr. Wellington
Koo being among the first to offer
congratulations on their safe
arrival. Lord Lytton, who look-
ed fairly well considering his
recent illness, when asked to
grant an interview to the many
newspaper representatives gath-
ered to meet him, courteously
intimated that he had nothing to
say and did not wish to be inter-
viewed.
Accompanied by Mayor Wu and
headed by two European police
officers on motor cycles, Lord
Lytton immediately drove to the
Cathay Hotel. Other members
of the party followed in the same
manner. Invitations to re-
ceptions were refused on account
of the indisposition of the Chair-
man of the Commission.

To Leave To-Day
Lord Lytton spent the night
quietly at the Hotel and he, to-
gether with his fellow commis-
sioners will board the s.s. Gange
this morning, the tender leaving
the Customs Jetty at 8.30. Dr.
Wellington Koo is also proceeding
to France by the same boat.
The full story of the departure
from Peiping and the early morn-
ing signing of the historic docu-
ment (still being kept secret) is
told in the Reuter telegrams
which follow:—

Commissioners Leave
PEIPING, Sept. 4.—Lord Lytton,
accompanied by General F. R.
McCoy the American member of
the League Commission, and Mrs.
McCoy, Count Mare-Scotti, the
Italian member, Mr. W. H. Donald,
adviser to Marshal Chang Hsueh-
liang and the Hon. W. W. Astor,
Lord Lytton's secretary, hopped
off at 10 o'clock this morning in
the Marshal's 'plane on their way
to Shanghai.
Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang per-
sonally saw the party off.—Reuter.

Historic Ceremony
PEIPING, Sept. 4. — At 8
o'clock this morning, the Lytton
report, for which the whole world
has been waiting, was signed in
the German hospital here. Lord
Lytton was the first to affix his
signature, the other four members
of the Commission followed him.
The ceremony took place on the
balcony of the hospital where
Lord Lytton has been lying since
he arrived here from Japan on
July 20.
Besides all the members of the
Commission nearly the whole of
the Secretariat was present as
well as members of the hospital
staff and other interested specta-
tors.

Staff Works All Night
The signing of the report this
morning represents the outcome of
a special spurt to complete the
document before the departure of
Lord Lytton for Shanghai this
morning. Members of the Commis-
sion worked until midnight last
night and then retired to bed in
view of to-day's long flight. But
the staff of the Secretariat con-
tinued its labours until dawn,
completing a report which is be-
lieved to comprise 400 pages run-
ning to more than 100,000 words.
It marks the culmination of
labours begun last January when
the Commission held its first meet-
ing in Geneva prior to sailing for
New York.
With the signing of the report
this morning the Commission as
such, ceased to exist, its last
official act being to pass a vote
of thanks to the Commission's
medical officer, Dr. Juvelet, who
has tended the health of members
during their extensive travels.
Before leaving the hospital this
morning, Lord Lytton personally
expressed his gratitude to Dr.
Paul Krieg, senior hospital doctor
whose patient he has been since
he returned to Peiping.
Drive To Aerodrome
Lord Lytton, who has scarcely
been out of doors since he return-
ed from Japan, enjoyed the drive
from the hospital to the aviation
field at Chingze. First he motored
through the busy streets of the
ancient city, out of the historic
gate and then through the pleas-
ant countryside, looking its best in
sunny autumn weather. The route
was lined by special guards drawn
from a crack cavalry regiment,
and also detachment of police
dotted along the road to the aero-
drome.
The mounted men gave a pic-
turesque touch, standing motion-

《字林西报》，1932年9月5日，星期一

李顿勋爵及其一行
由北平乘飞机抵沪

历史性文件于清晨签署的全部经过；李顿勋爵称世人须对已完成之工作作出评判

一行将乘“恒河”号轮船赴欧
今晨离沪

国际联盟满洲调查团团长李顿勋爵，在麦考伊将军及夫人、阿尔德罗万迪伯爵及其随员陪同下，昨日午后乘坐张学良元帅的三引擎福特式飞机，经六小时飞行从北平抵达虹桥机场，目的是登上将于今日清晨启航赴欧的“恒河”号（s.s. Gange）轮船。调查团报告书仅于昨日清晨在北平完成并签署，调查团的任务现已结束。李顿勋爵昨日下午拒绝接受任何报纸采访，在此间受到正式欢迎后，前往华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel），他将于今晨从该处登船。

凌晨1时，
在公安局长温应星将军辖下的公安局警察严密守卫着虹桥机场。现场还有若干中国士兵站岗，以及来自上海公共租界工部局的警务人员。
当这架巨型客机于下午3时50分抵达时（该机上午10时离开北平），机场至少有200人前来欢迎这些尊贵的访客。在场人士中可见市长吴铁城、顾维钧博士（新任中国驻法公使）、齐亚诺伯爵（意大利公使）、外交部次长刘宗峙先生、上海总商会代表以及许多中外知名人士。

热烈欢迎
李顿勋爵及机上其他八名乘客受到了热烈欢迎，吴市长和顾维钧博士是最早祝贺他们平安抵达的人士之一。鉴于近期患病，李顿勋爵的气色看起来相当不错，当被要求向聚集迎接他的众多报社代表发表谈话时，他礼貌地表示无话可说，不愿接受采访。

李顿勋爵在吴市长陪同下，由两名骑摩托车的欧洲巡捕开道，立即驱车前往华懋饭店。代表团其他成员也随后以同样方式前往。由于调查团主席身体不适，所有参加招待会的邀请均被谢绝。

今日离沪
李顿勋爵在饭店安静地度过了一夜，他与各位委员将于今晨登上“恒河”号轮船，接驳船将于8时30分离开海关码头。顾维钧博士也将乘同一艘船前往法国。
关于从北平出发及清晨签署历史性文件（目前仍保密）的全部经过，详见以下路透社电文：—

委员们离开
北平，9月4日。—李顿勋爵在国际联盟委员会美国委员F. R. 麦考伊将军及麦考伊夫人、意大利委员马雷-斯科蒂伯爵、张学良元帅顾问W. H. 唐纳德先生以及李顿勋爵秘书W. W. 阿斯特勋爵陪同下，于今晨10时乘坐元帅的飞机起飞，前往上海。
张学良元帅亲自送行。—路透社。

历史性仪式
北平，9月4日。—举世翘首以待的李顿报告书，于今晨8时在此间的德国医院签署。李顿勋爵首先签字，调查团其他四名委员随后签署。仪式在医院阳台举行，李顿勋爵自7月20日从日本抵达此处后一直在此休养。

除调查团全体成员外，秘书处几乎全体人员均在场，医院工作人员及其他感兴趣的旁观者也在场。

工作人员通宵工作
今晨签署报告书标志着为在李顿勋爵今晨启程赴沪前完成文件而进行的特别冲刺的结果。调查团成员工作至昨晚午夜，鉴于今日长途飞行，随后便去休息。但秘书处工作人员继续工作直至黎明，完成了一份据信长达400页、逾10万字的报告。
这标志着始于去年一月的工作达到高潮，当时调查团在驶往纽约之前于日内瓦举行了首次会议。
随着今晨报告书的签署，调查团作为一个机构已不复存在，其最后一项官方行动是通过一项决议，感谢调查团医务官朱夫莱医生（Dr. Juvelet），他在成员们广泛旅行期间照料他们的健康。
今晨离开医院前，李顿勋爵亲自向高级住院医生保罗·克里格医生（Dr. Paul Krieg）表达谢意，自返回北平以来，他一直由其诊治。

驱车前往机场
自日本返回后几乎未曾外出的李顿勋爵，享受了从医院到静子（Chingze，音译）航空场的车程。他先乘车穿过古城繁忙的街道，驶出历史悠久的城门，然后穿过宜人的乡村，在秋日明媚的阳光下景色宜人。路线两旁排列着从精锐骑兵团抽调的特卫，沿途通往机场的道路上还分布着分遣警察部队。

骑兵队员们静止不动地站在路边，

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 5, 1932

less by the roadside, silhouetted against the skyline or half hidden by fields of tall kaoliang. The road had already been watered by blue clad coolies from the city so that the travellers should not be worried by dust, and the stream of motor cars preceding and following Lord Lytton and his party made good time to the aviation field.
Plane Tuned Up
There Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang's splendid Ford 'plane was ready for the take off, tuned up ready for the flight to Shanghai. A large assembly of people gathered to say farewell, among those present being Mr. E. M. B. Ingram, British Charge d'Affaires, Dr. Trautman, the German Minister, Chevalier Anfuso, Italian Charge and other diplomats, Generals Wan Fu-lin, Yu Hsuch-chung and Chou Ta-wen, members of the Commission and the staff of the Secretariat.
Upon the arrival of Lord Lytton, several companies of Chinese troops were drawn up smartly to attention and the band struck up a tune. Among the first to be greeted by Lord Lytton were Sister Superior Schornlevrl, Sister Ernst and Sister Ottmg, Sister Ottma was Lord Lytton's nurse in the hospital and she and her colleagues were conspicuous among the crowd by their white uniforms.
Dr. Trautman expressed the pride and pleasure of the German hospital having had Lord Lytton as a patient, and Lord Lytton in the course of a smiling reply, paid tribute to the institution. He owed a great debt to Germany in this respect although still a little weak, he felt better than he had felt at any time since his arrival in China, and was enjoying the beautiful sunny weather.
Marshal Chang Happy
Shortly before 10 o'clock, Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang arrived and chatted with Lord Lytton and other distinguished people. The Marshal seemed in a happy mood and personally escorted the travellers to the plane and saw them comfortable. There were nine passengers, Lord Lytton, General and Mrs. McCoy, Count Aldrovandi, Herr von Kotze, M. Charrere, Mr. W. Astor, Lieutenant Biddle, and Mr. W. H. Donald. The 'plane was piloted by Mr. Perry Hutton, who carried as mechanic, Mr. Carl Kjus.
Sharp at 10 o'clock the plane took off amid much cheering and waving of hats, skimmed the field and circled over the watching crowd before finally speeding south. In view of the perfect flying weather the 'plane was expected to make fast time completing the journey in possibly less than six hours.
Final Interview
Interviewed just before he left, Lord Lytton declared that he really had nothing to say beyond the fact that the report was signed adding with a smile, "and as a result I am now defunct." However, in response to questions he confirmed that the report was unanimous and said its contents were not being communicated to China and Japan at present, but would be released simultaneously to Geneva, Nanking, and Tokyo. Asked how the report was being conveyed to Geneva, Lord Lytton stated that the official copy was going via Peiping reading a decision as to the quickest method of getting it to Europe, and he hint-

ed that possibly it would be taken part of the way by air.
Lord Lytton's attention was drawn to Japan's intention of recognizing "Manchukuo," and asked whether he could say if such intention would modify the effectiveness of his report, replied with a smile with which he parries all leading questions as to the contents of the report.
A Starting Point
When reminded of a previous interview in which he had stated that the aim of the Commission was to find a basis for negotiation and when asked if this aim had been fulfilled, he replied that the Commission had been appointed with the object of indicating to the League Council a possible starting point for finding a way out of the impasse in which these two countries found themselves. Asked if he felt that the Commission had succeeded in doing this in their report, Lord Lytton shrugged his shoulders and replied that this was a matter for others to judge.
Lord Lytton also gave interviews to Chinese and Japanese journalists, returning tactful answers to all awkward questions such as those asking his opinion of conditions in China, to which he replied that he hoped some time to return to the Far East a "free man" when he could enjoy the beauties of the country.
Personal Plans
Lord Lytton's personal plans are to land in Venice from the s.s. Gange, where he probably will be met by his daughter, Lady Hermanie Cobbold, who lives in Milan. After visiting Milan Lord Lytton will proceed to England and probably will be met in London by his wife.
The French and German members of the Commission, General Claudel and Dr. Schnee intend to leave Harbin on September 12, travelling to Europe via Siberia. On account of conditions in north Manchuria they possibly will fly from Harbin to either Tsitsihar or Manchuli, accompanied by the remaining members of their staff and Secretariat.—Reuter.
Journey Of Report
LONDON, Sept. 4.—The "Sunday Times" learns to-day that the Lytton Commission report is expected to reach the Secretary-General of the League of Nations in the course of the next ten days. Copies will probably be formally distributed to the governments concerned so that they may have the opportunity of studying it before discussing recommendations at Geneva.
Via Siberia
General Claudel and Dr. Schnee left Peiping this afternoon for Dairen en route to Harbin.—Reuter.

Departed for Europe
by S.S. Gange on 5/9/32
JBR 5/9.

《字林西报》，1932年9月5日，星期一

映衬在天际线下，或半隐于高大的高粱地里，构成了一幅如画的景象。来自城里的身穿蓝衣的苦力早已洒水湿润道路，以免旅行者受尘土困扰，而在李顿勋爵及其一行前后行驶的轿车车队也迅速抵达了航空场。

飞机调试完毕
此时，张学良元帅那架漂亮的福特飞机已准备好起飞，经过调试，准备飞往上海。大批人群聚集告别，在场人士包括英国代办E. M. B. 英格拉姆先生、德国公使特劳特曼博士、意大利代办安富索骑士以及其他外交官，万福麟、于学忠和周大文将军，调查团成员及秘书处工作人员。
李顿勋爵抵达时，几连中国军队整齐列队立正，军乐队奏乐。肖恩莱弗尔修女院长（Sister Superior Schornlevrl，音译）、恩斯特修女（Sister Ernst，音译）和奥特明修女（Sister Ottmg，音译）是首批受到李顿勋爵问候的人，奥特明修女曾是李顿勋爵在医院的护士，她们和同事身着白色制服，在人群中格外显眼。
特劳特曼博士表达了德国医院曾收治李顿勋爵为病人的自豪与喜悦，李顿勋爵在微笑作答时对该机构给予了赞誉。他表示在这方面欠德国很大的人情，虽然仍有些虚弱，但他感觉比自抵达中国以来的任何时候都要好，并且很享受这美好的晴朗天气。

张元帅很高兴
接近10时，张学良元帅抵达，并与李顿勋爵及其他贵宾交谈。元帅似乎心情愉快，亲自护送旅客至飞机旁并安顿好他们。乘客共九人：李顿勋爵、麦考伊将军及夫人、阿尔德罗万迪伯爵、冯·科策先生（Herr von Kotze，音译）、夏雷尔先生（M. Charrere，音译）、W. 阿斯特先生、比德尔中尉（Lieutenant Biddle，音译）以及W. H. 唐纳德先生。飞机由佩里·赫顿先生（Mr. Perry Hutton，音译）驾驶，机械师为卡尔·克尤斯先生（Mr. Carl Kjus，音译）。
10时整，飞机在欢呼声和挥帽致意中起飞，掠过场地，在围观人群上空盘旋一圈，最后向南疾驰而去。鉴于飞行天气完美，预计飞机将快速完成旅程，可能少于六小时。

最后采访
在离开前接受采访时，李顿勋爵声明，除了报告书已签署这一事实外，他确实无话可说，并微笑着补充道：“因此，我现在算是‘卸任’了。”然而，在回应提问时，他确认报告书是一致通过的，并表示其内容目前未通报给中国和日本，但将同时向日内瓦、南京和东京发布。当被问及报告书如何送往日内瓦时，李顿勋爵表示，正本将经由北平发送，正在决定将其运往欧洲的最快方法，他暗示可能会部分路段采用空运。

有人提请李顿勋爵注意日本意图承认“满洲国”，并询问他能否说明此意图是否会削弱其报告书的效力，他微笑着回答，以此回避所有关于报告书内容的诱导性问题。

一个起点
当被提醒他在之前的一次采访中曾表示，调查团的目的是寻找谈判基础，并被问及此目标是否已实现时，他回答说，任命调查团的目的是向国联理事会指出一个可能的起点，以寻找摆脱这两个国家所处僵局的出路。当被问及他是否认为调查团在报告中成功做到了这一点时，李顿勋爵耸了耸肩，回答说这是由他人来评判的事情。
李顿勋爵还接受了中国和日本记者的采访，对所有棘手问题都给予了得体的回答，例如询问他对中国局势的看法，他回答说希望将来能以“自由人”的身份回到远东，届时可以欣赏这个国家的美景。

个人计划
李顿勋爵的个人计划是乘“恒河”号轮船在威尼斯登陆，住在那不勒斯（原文为Milan，米兰，但其女住在米兰，此处逻辑稍显混乱，依原文译作米兰）的女儿赫尔曼妮·科博尔德女爵士（Lady Hermanie Cobbold）可能会去接他。访问米兰后，李顿勋爵将前往英国，其夫人可能在伦敦迎接他。
调查团的法国和德国成员克洛代尔将军（General Claudel，音译）和施内博士（Dr. Schnee，音译）打算于9月12日离开哈尔滨，经西伯利亚前往欧洲。鉴于北满的局势，他们可能会在剩余的工作人员和秘书处成员的陪同下，从哈尔滨飞往齐齐哈尔或满洲里。—路透社。

报告书的旅程
伦敦，9月4日。—《星期日泰晤士报》今日获悉，李顿调查团报告书预计在未来十天内送达国际联盟秘书长。副本可能会正式分发给有关各国政府，以便它们在日内瓦讨论建议之前有机会进行研究。

经西伯利亚
克洛代尔将军和施内博士今天下午离开北平前往大连，途中转往哈尔滨。—路透社。

于1932年9月5日乘“恒河”号轮船启程赴欧
JBR 9月5日。

THE NORTH-CHINA SUNDAY NEWS, SEPTEMBER 4, 1932

COMPLETION OF LEAGUE
COMMISSION REPORT

Members Attach Signatures to Result Of
Their Investigation

LORD LYTTON DUE HERE TO-DAY

Sealed Copies Left Behind For China And
Japan: Special League Session

Peking, Sept. 3.
REUTER learns to-day that the report of the Lytton Commission is unanimous. Completed on Thursday afternoon, the report was at once stencilled, after which it was read over by the members of the Commission, who spent the whole day on this task.
The members made various corrections and the report was again given to the typist, who sat up all night typing the final copies. Lord Lytton and his colleagues are now reading these copies and it is expected that they will sign them before leaving by 'plane for Shanghai. Each copy will bear five signatures.
The contents of the report are not being communicated to China and Japan, but two sealed copies are being left behind, one for the Japanese Government and the other for the Chinese Government, to be opened on the same day and at the same hour as the report is released at Geneva.

LORD LYTTON ARRIVING BY AEROPLANE

Lord Lytton is leaving for Shanghai in Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang's luxurious air liner at 10 o'clock to-morrow morning. He will be accompanied by General F. R. McCoy, the American member of the Commission, and Mrs. McCoy; Count Marescotti, the Italian member; Mr. W. H. Donald, adviser to Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang, and the Hon. W. W. Astor, Lord Lytton's secretary.
General Claudel, the French member of the Commission, and Dr. Schnee, the German member, intend travelling via Siberia.
Foreign messages from Harbin state that in view of the interruption of communications west of Harbin, the Japanese authorities at Harbin have offered to place 'planes at the disposal of General Claudel, Dr. Schnee and any officials of the Commission returning via Siberia. If the offer is accepted, Japanese 'planes will take the party from Harbin to Manchuli, on the Sino-Russian frontier.
The suggestion made by the Japanese comes as a sequel to confirmation of the reports that "irregulars" have captured Anta, completely interrupting communication with Manchuli.
The messages add that the Japanese forces are operating against the "irregulars," who are stated to be under the command of General Li Hai-cheng.
Farewell Call on Marshal Chang
Lord Lytton and the other members of the League of Nations Commission paid a farewell courtesy visit this afternoon upon Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang.
Their aeroplane will not make any stop en route to-morrow but will make a direct flight to Shanghai from Peking. They will probably be about five and a half hours on the journey, and as they are due to leave about ten o'clock they should reach Shanghai between 3 and 4 p.m. on Sunday afternoon.—Reuter.

SPECIAL SESSION FOR
REPORT

London, Sept. 3.
It is understood that the Report of the Commission of Enquiry headed by Lord Lytton, which has just been completed, will not be considered at the forthcoming session of the Assembly of the League at Geneva, but a special session may be called at the beginning of November to deal with it.—Reuter.

Unfavourable To Japan?

Peking, Sept. 3.
The final report of the League of Nations Inquiry Commission headed by Lord Lytton was completed at midnight last night and was being signed by commission members this afternoon before being dispatched to Geneva.
The conclusion of the report consisted of a brief summing-up of only two or three typewritten sheets, it was learned.

《华北星期新闻》，1932年9月4日

国联调查团报告完成

成员在调查结果上签署姓名

李顿勋爵预计今日抵沪

留交中日两国密封副本：国联特别会议

北平，9月3日。
路透社今日获悉，李顿调查团的报告一致通过。报告于周四下午完成，随即进行油印，此后由调查团成员通读全文，他们整日皆致力于此工作。
成员们作了多处修正，报告再次交给打字员，后者通宵打字以制作最终副本。李顿勋爵及其同僚目前正在阅读这些副本，预计他们将在乘飞机前往上海之前签署副本。每份副本上将会有五个签名。
报告内容并未向中日两国通报，但留下了两份密封副本，一份给日本政府，另一份给中国政府，待报告在日内瓦发布之同日同时开启。

李顿勋爵乘飞机抵达

李顿勋爵将于明日上午10时，乘坐张学良将军的豪华客机前往上海。陪同他的有美国籍调查团成员麦考伊（F. R. McCoy）将军及麦考伊夫人；意大利籍调查团成员马雷斯科蒂（Marescotti）伯爵；张学良将军顾问唐纳德（W. H. Donald）先生，以及李顿勋爵的秘书阿斯特（W. W. Astor）阁下。
法国籍调查团成员克劳德尔（Claudel）将军和德国籍调查团成员施内（Schnee）博士打算经西伯利亚旅行。
来自哈尔滨的外电称，鉴于哈尔滨以西通讯中断，哈尔滨日本当局已表示愿提供飞机，供经西伯利亚返回的克劳德尔将军、施内博士及调查团任何官员使用。如接受该提议，日本飞机将把一行人从哈尔滨送往中俄边境的满洲里。
日方的建议是在证实“非正规军”已占领安达、完全切断与满洲里通讯的报道之后提出的。
电文补充说，日军正在对据称由李海城将军指挥的“非正规军”采取行动。
辞行拜访张将军
李顿勋爵及国联调查团其他成员于今天下午礼节性拜会了张学良将军，以示辞行。
他们的飞机明日途中不停留，将从北平直飞上海。航程大约需要五个半小时，由于预计约十点钟出发，他们应于周日下午3点至4点之间抵达上海。——路透社。

为审议报告召开特别会议

伦敦，9月3日。
据悉，刚刚完成的由李顿勋爵率领的调查委员会报告，不会在即将召开的日内瓦国联大会会议上审议，但可能会在11月初召开特别会议来处理此事。——路透社。

对日本不利？

北平，9月3日。
由李顿勋爵率领的国联调查委员会的最终报告于昨晚午夜完成，委员会成员于今天下午在将其发往日内瓦之前正在签署报告。
据悉，报告的结论部分仅为两至三页打字纸的简短总结。

THE NORTH-CHINA SUNDAY NEWS, SEPTEMBER 4, 1932

Lord Lytton's first desire was said to have been to base the conclusion purely upon jurisprudence, which would make the case quite unfavourable to Japan.
Due to efforts by General Claudel, French member of the commission, this plan was somewhat amended, it was said. The report was understood to be unfavourable to Japan in many points, however.—United Press.

Submission To Geneva
Peking, Sept. 3.
The report of the League of Nations Commission of Inquiry which is to be signed to-day will be carried by Lord Lytton as far as Singapore and will be then carried by the Dutch mail service aeroplane to Europe, it has been decided.
As the Italian liner Gange, on which Lord Lytton and the party will travel, is to arrive at Singapore September 10 and the aeroplane takes eight days from there to Europe, the report is expected to arrive in Geneva on the 18th or 19th of this month.—Rengo.

League's Programme
Geneva, Sept. 3.
In the course of this month the League of Nations will resume its activities, which were, for the greater part at a standstill during the summer holidays, after the adjournment of the Disarmament Conference in July last. The ordinary annual meeting of the League General Assembly which, according to the schedule was to be held on September 12, was postponed until September 26. This session is not likely to be of a great importance. It will last two weeks instead of three or four, which it usually requires. However, everything would be entirely different, should it be decided to discuss the report of Lord Lytton's Commission for Manchuria, during this month.
However, authoritative experts believe that this discussion will be taken up in the course of a special meeting of the extraordinary assembly which will be informed of the case during October or November. Under these circumstances, the Assembly session, which will meet on Sept. 26, will merely be of a formal character, and will give an occasion for reviewing the current issues.
On September 22, the representative of Ireland, who will probably be Mr. Eamon de Valera, President of the Irish Free State, will open the 68th session of the League Council. The programme of this session is of no special interest at present. However, the course of events, and notably the German demarche for obtaining equality of armaments, the Bolivo-Paraguayan conflict, and the eventual result of the Stresa Conference, may eventually bring certain changes on this programme.

Some Important Questions
The principal questions which will be submitted to the League Council are the cessation of the British mandate on Irak, the report of the Studying Committee on the questions concerning public works of international character, the financial situation in Greece and the demand for financial assistance made by Rumania.
The studying committee for Public Works and of national industrial development will meet on September 7. This Committee will examine the possibilities of realising the great projects of international public works, which were proposed by M. Albert Thomas, the late Director of the International Labour Bureau, with the purpose of coping with the unemployment.
On September 19, a meeting of the League Finance Committee will take place. The Committee will study the financial position of Rumania, Bulgaria and Greece.
Finally the Presidium of the Disarmament Conference will meet on September 21. It will be recalled that the resolution which was voted before the adjournment of this Conference has charged its Presidium to draft the texts of two projects or resolutions concerning the questions, on which an agreement has already been reached.

Arms Discussion
Furthermore, the Presidium of the Arms Conference will also have to examine in conjunction with the representatives of the interested powers, certain points demanding a closer study, in order to be able to come to some definite conclusions as soon as the Conference's General Committee will resume its work.
The questions which will be thus studied are those of the effectives, of the limitation of national defense expenses, the regulation of the commerce and manufacturing of arms.
It will be recalled that the Presidium can fix with a month's notice the date of the next meeting of the Disarmament Conference.
It goes without saying, that the recent demarche made by Germany in Paris, claiming the freedom of armaments in derogation of the Versailles Treaty, will have a certain repercussion on the work at Geneva.—Havas.

《华北星期新闻》，1932年9月4日

据说李顿勋爵最初的愿望是纯粹依据法理来制定结论，这将使案情对日本极为不利。
据说，由于调查团法国成员克劳德尔将军的努力，这一计划做了一些修改。然而，据了解，报告在许多方面对日本不利。——合众社。

提交日内瓦
北平，9月3日。
已决定，今日将签署的国联调查委员会报告将由李顿勋爵携带至新加坡，然后由荷兰邮政服务飞机运往欧洲。
由于李顿勋爵一行将乘坐的意大利轮船“恒河”号（Gange）将于9月10日抵达新加坡，而飞机从那里飞往欧洲需时八天，预计报告将于本月18日或19日抵达日内瓦。——联合通讯社。

国联日程安排
日内瓦，9月3日。
在本月内，国际联盟将恢复其活动，这些活动在去年7月裁军会议休会后的暑假期间大部分处于停滞状态。原定于9月12日举行的国联大会常会已推迟至9月26日。此次会议可能并不十分重要。会期将为两周，而非通常所需的三或四周。然而，如果决定在本月讨论李顿满洲调查团的报告，情况将完全不同。
不过，权威专家认为，这一讨论将在10月或11月召开的特别大会特别会议上进行，届时将向会议通报此案。在这种情况下，将于9月26日召开的大会会议仅具有形式性质，并将提供审查当前议题的机会。
9月22日，爱尔兰代表（可能是爱尔兰自由邦总统埃蒙·德·瓦莱拉先生）将主持国联理事会第68次会议。目前该会议的议程并无特别引人关注之处。然而，事态的发展，特别是德国为争取军备平等所采取的行动、玻利维亚-巴拉圭冲突，以及斯特雷萨会议的可能结果，最终可能会对该议程带来某些变化。

若干重要问题
将提交国联理事会的主要问题包括：终止英国对伊拉克的委任统治、关于具有国际性质的公共工程问题的研究委员会报告、希腊的财政状况以及罗马尼亚提出的财政援助请求。
公共工程及国家工业发展研究委员会将于9月7日开会。该委员会将审查实现大型国际公共工程项目的可能性，这些项目由已故国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯先生提出，旨在应对失业问题。
9月19日，国联财政委员会将举行会议。委员会将研究罗马尼亚、保加利亚和希腊的财政状况。
最后，裁军会议主席团将于9月21日开会。需指出的是，在该会议休会前通过的决议已授权其主席团起草有关已达成协议的问题的两项草案或决议文本。

军备讨论
此外，裁军会议主席团还将与有关大国代表共同审查某些需要更深入研究的要点，以便在裁军会议全体委员会恢复工作时能够尽快得出明确结论。
因此将被研究的问题包括：兵力数额、限制国防开支、管制武器贸易和制造。
需指出的是，主席团可提前一个月通知确定裁军会议下次会议的日期。
不言而喻，德国最近在巴黎采取的、要求违背《凡尔赛条约》享有军备自由的行动，将对日内瓦的工作产生一定影响。——哈瓦斯社。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, MARCH 28, 1932
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 3380.
Date 4 / 4 / 32.

Nanking Astir
As Committee
Reaches City
Streets Strongly Guard-
ed By Police, Good
Order Maintained

STREAMS OF STUDENTS,
OTHER DELEGATES

“Chinese Would Rather Die
With Honour” Than Live
Under Japanese Rule

At 10 o’clock on Saturday morning, members of the League Manchurian Commission, including Lord Lytton, chairman, went ashore at Nanking and proceeded to the quarters of the Officers Moral Endeavour Society. The city was gay with flags in honour of the visitors and streams of students and delegates from various public organizations participated in welcoming the Commission. Shops were profusely plastered with messages of welcome and propaganda messages, one of which was, “The Chinese would rather die with honour than live under Japanese militarism.”

NANKING, March 26.—Members of the League Manchurian Commission, including Lord Lytton, chairman, arrived in Nanking at 10 o’clock this morning in the s.s. Tuckwo.

The steamer came in sight about 9.30. Contrary to expectations, she did not moor at the San Peh wharf but went farther upstream and anchored in the river. At the San Peh wharf was waiting a ferry boat with Dr. Lo Wen-kan, Foreign Minister, General Ku Chung-lun, General Chen Yi and Mr. Uyemura, Japanese Consul-General, Assistant.

When the Tuckwo went up stream, the ferryboat steamed up alongside and a gangway was put down between the vessels, allowing the officials to cross to welcome the commissioners.

At 10 o’clock the party came ashore and proceeded to the quarters of the Officers Moral Endeavour Society, there being a parade of 40 motor cars, the leading car containing Lord Lytton and Mr. Z. Ting, chief of the Nanking reception committee.

The Chungshan Road was lined with people and over it was built a decorated pailou bearing welcoming signs. The streets were strongly guarded by police and Boy Scouts, and good order was maintained.

The city is gay with flags today in honour of the Commission. From an early hour this morning, streams of students and delegates from various public organizations

were going towards Hsiakwan and to the Chungshan Road to take up positions to welcome the Commission.

Shops are plastered with messages of welcome and propaganda messages in English. The more popular ones read, “The Chinese would rather die with honour than live under Japanese militarism,” and “China supports the League for promoting peace and justice,” and “We want justice. Impartiality must be observed.”

Informal Reception

The reception accorded to the members of the Commission aboard the Tuckwo has quite informal. After the first greetings had been exchanged and a cordial welcome to Nanking had been extended to the Commissioners there was a general move for the shore.

Mr. Yoshida, Japanese assessor, and the members of his staff were the first to walk down the gangway to the ferry-boat. A few minutes later, Lord Lytton, Count Aldrovandi Marescotti, Dr. Lo Wen-kan, Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo, the Chinese assessor on the Commission, and Madame Wellington Koo appeared on the deck of the Tuckwo. At the gangway, Dr. Lo Wen-kan insisted that Lord Lytton should take precedence. Lord Lytton modestly declined the honour, and, after much insistence on both sides, Dr. Lo Wen-kan walked on to the ferry, followed by the other members of the party. The ferry boat then made its way to the San Peh wharf while the Tuckwo returned down stream and went alongside Messrs. Jardine Matheson’s regular wharf.

Ubiquitous Cameramen

As Lord Lytton was leaving the Tuckwo, he stood for a few moments to oblige a number of photographers who wished to take snapshots, and a number of good pictures were obtained. A strong wind was blowing, and the river, as a consequence, was choppy. A British destroyer lying off Hsiakwan sent a motor boat to stand by the Tuckwo to render any assistance that might be necessary, but its services were not required. No trouble or discomfort of any kind was experienced in the disembarkation.

Light refreshments were served on the ferry-boat and the short time occupied by the trip passed pleasantly in general conversation. When the San Peh wharf was reached, a Chinese naval band struck up a “snappy” tune and the gendarmes and police stationed at the entrance in honour of the visitors stood smartly to attention. The welcome had been well organized and all details were carried through with military precision. A further few minutes’ halt was again necessary, however, to satisfy the ubiquitous cameramen, but on this occasion a news-reel talking picture was taken for presentation in many dozens of Chinese cinemas. Following this interlude, the members of the Commission, accompanied by the Chinese reception delegation, proceeded direct to the headquarters of the Officers’ Moral Endeavour Association, where they are staying.

《上海泰晤士报》，1932年3月28日，星期一
上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与特别科登记处。
编号 D 3380。
日期 1932年4月4日。

南京轰动
委员会
抵达该市
街道由警察严密守卫，秩序良好

学生人流及其他代表团

“中国人宁愿光荣赴死”也不愿在日本统治下苟活

周六上午10时，包括主席李顿勋爵（Lord Lytton）在内的国联满洲调查团成员在南京登陆，并前往军官励志社（Officers Moral Endeavour Society）驻地。全城张灯结彩，悬挂旗帜以欢迎来访者，来自各公共团体的学生流和代表团参与了欢迎委员会的活动。商店贴满了欢迎标语和宣传口号，其中一条写道：“中国人宁愿光荣赴死，也不愿生活在日本军国主义之下。”

南京，3月26日电。—包括主席李顿勋爵在内的国联满洲调查团成员，于今日上午10时乘“太古”轮（s.s. Tuckwo）抵达南京。

该轮船约在9时30分进入视野。出乎意料的是，它并未在三北码头（San Peh wharf）停靠，而是继续向上游行驶并在江中抛锚。三北码头停泊着一艘渡轮，上面有外交部长罗文干博士、顾祝同将军、陈仪将军以及日本副总领事上村先生（Mr. Uyemura）。

当“太古”轮溯流而上时，渡轮驶至其旁侧，两船之间搭起跳板，官员们得以通过跳板登船欢迎调查团委员。

10时，一行人登陆并前往军官励志社驻地，共有40辆汽车组成的车队随行，头车内坐着李顿勋爵和南京接待委员会主任丁先生（Mr. Z. Ting）。

中山路两旁挤满了人群，路上搭建了一座装饰着欢迎标语的牌楼。街道由警察和童子军严密守卫，秩序井然。

为向调查团致敬，今日全城旗帜飘扬。从今天清晨开始，来自各公共团体的学生流和代表团

便纷纷前往下关和中山路，占据位置以欢迎调查团。

商店贴满了英文的欢迎标语和宣传口号。较为流行的标语包括：“中国人宁愿光荣赴死，也不愿生活在日本军国主义之下”，“中国支持国联以促进和平与正义”，以及“我们要正义。必须保持公正。”

非正式接待

在“太古”轮上对调查团成员进行的接待相当非正式。在互致问候并向委员们表示对南京的热烈欢迎后，众人普遍准备上岸。

日本参事官吉田先生（Mr. Yoshida）及其职员成员最先走下跳板登上渡轮。几分钟后，李顿勋爵、阿尔德罗万迪·马雷斯科蒂伯爵（Count Aldrovandi Marescotti）、罗文干博士、调查团中方参事顾维钧博士（Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo）以及顾维钧夫人出现在“太古”轮的甲板上。在跳板处，罗文干博士坚持请李顿勋爵先行。李顿勋爵谦逊地谢绝了这一荣誉，经过双方再三坚持，罗文干博士走上渡轮，其他随行成员紧随其后。随后渡轮驶往三北码头，而“太古”轮则顺流而下，停靠在怡和洋行（Messrs. Jardine Matheson）的常规码头旁。

无处不在的摄影师

当李顿勋爵离开“太古”轮时，他站立片刻以满足多位希望拍摄快照的摄影师的要求，从而获得了一些精彩的照片。当时大风劲吹，导致江面波涛汹涌。一艘停泊在下关附近的英国驱逐舰派出一艘摩托艇在“太古”轮旁待命，以备提供可能需要的援助，但并未用到其服务。登陆过程中未经历任何麻烦或不适。

渡轮上供应了茶点，短暂的航程在一般的交谈中愉快地度过。到达三北码头时，中国海军乐队奏起了一首“轻快”的曲调，入口处为向访客致敬而驻守的宪兵和警察精神抖擞地立正敬礼。欢迎活动组织周密，所有细节均以军事般的精确度执行。然而，为了迎合无处不在的摄影师，又不得不停留几分钟，但此次拍摄的是一部新闻有声电影，将在中国数十家电影院放映。插曲过后，调查团成员在中国接待代表团的陪同下，直接前往他们下榻的军官励志协会总部。

pages.en:
A Thrilling Rescue
Reuters correspondent greeted the members of the League Commission on the ferry-boat. They did not speak of the duties which lay before them, but gave a thrilling description of the rescue by the Tuckwo of three Chinese from a junk which foundered in the storm that raged on the river about an hour before the Tuckwo reached Nanking. It is believed that two other Chinese, who were on the junk when it sank, were drowned.

Reuter was informed that Mr. T. V. Soong, Minister of Finance, had originally expected to travel to Nanking by the Tuckwo, but he was unavoidably detained, and it is thought probable that he will come to Nanking to-night by motor car via Hangchow.

The Tuckwo's arrival so early in the morning was entirely unexpected. Lord Lytton told those present at the Officers' Moral Endeavour Association that he himself did not expect to reach Nanking until 3 o'clock in the afternoon. As the result of this early arrival, many Government leaders were not present at the Hsiakwan wharf to welcome the Commission, and what was perhaps of even greater immediate importance, the commissariat department of the Officers' Moral Endeavour Association was caught entirely unprepared. It had made adequate arrangements for dinner this evening, but there was nothing for tiffin. However, a few messengers sent here and there followed by feverish activity in the kitchen, and all difficulties were quickly overcome.

Mr. Yoshida, Japanese assessor, left the Commission near the Drum Tower and proceeded to the Japanese Consulate, where he will stay with the members of his staff while in Nanking.

Stretching A Point
As an indication that the Chinese authorities intend to do their utmost to entertain the members of the League Commission hospitably, the Officers' Moral Endeavour Association has broken a strict rule of the club by giving the commissioners liberty to smoke and drink on the premises. This has never before been allowed, even military commanders and Government leaders not being granted such liberties. Special offices have also been prepared for the Commission so that they may have every facility for carrying on their work during their stay in Nanking.

Major-General Wang Jin-lin, of the Officers' Moral Endeavour Association, personally welcomed Lord Lytton and Count Marescotti at the entrance to the Association's building, and they were subsequently introduced to Mr. Hsu Mo, Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs. The comfortable reception hall was placed at the disposal of the Commission and here tea was served and musical entertainment provided.

May Go To Hankow
Mr. Hsu Mo, in an interview with Reuter, stated that no arrangements had been made for the entertainment of the Commission either this afternoon or this evening, and the opportunity would be given to them to rest. The members of the League Commission themselves spoke this morning of the possibility of proceeding to Hankow from Nanking, but nothing definite has been decided in this respect. Some of the staff of the Foreign Ministry, however, are proceeding to Hankow to make the necessary preparations for the Commission's trip up-river.

The Government received a telegram from Yihsin this afternoon stating that General McCoy, General Claudel and Dr. Schnee left for Nanking at 1.30 p.m. and are expected to arrive at Tongshan at 4.30. As they are not stopping at Tongshan, it is probable that they will reach Nanking between five and six o'clock.

Lord Lytton and Count Aldrovandi Marescotti were the guests of Dr. and Madame Wellington Koo at tiffin at the house in the Ministry of Railways, where Dr. Koo and his wife are staying.

Madame Koo was the centre of attraction on board the Tuckwo, and as soon as she landed in Nanking, she was immediately surrounded by a veritable army of American camera men. Hundreds of photographs were taken of her and of her four cute looking Pekinese dogs, but Madame Koo laughingly submitted to the ordeal. Her charming personality quickly establishes her as a favourite in all circles.—Reuter.

Other Members Arrive
March 27.—General McCoy, General Claudel and Dr. Schnee arrived at Nanking at 7.30 this evening.—Reuter.
pages.zh:
惊险救援

路透社记者在渡轮上 greeted（迎接）了国联调查团成员。他们并未谈及摆在他们面前的职责，而是生动描述了“太古”轮从一艘舢板中救出三名中国人的惊险过程，该舢板在“太古”轮抵达南京前约一小时在江上肆虐的风暴中沉没。据信，舢板沉没时在其上的另外两名中国人已溺水身亡。

据告知路透社，财政部长宋子文先生（Mr. T. V. Soong）原计划乘“太古”轮前往南京，但因故被耽搁，预计他今晚将经杭州乘汽车抵达南京。

“太古”轮如此早抵完全出乎意料。李顿勋爵告诉军官励志协会的在场人士，他自己原本预计下午3点才能抵达南京。由于提前抵达，许多政府领导人未能前往下关码头欢迎调查团，而或许更为重要的即时影响是，军官励志协会的膳食部门完全措手不及。他们已为今晚的晚宴做了充分安排，但却没有准备午餐。不过，几名信差四处奔走，随后厨房内一阵忙碌，所有困难很快得以克服。

日本参事官吉田先生在鼓楼附近离开调查团，前往日本领事馆，他在南京期间将与职员成员一同住在那里。

破例通融

作为中国当局意图尽其所能热情款待国联调查团成员的一个迹象，军官励志协会打破了俱乐部的一项严格规定，允许委员们在会所内吸烟和饮酒。此前从未允许过此类行为，即使是军事指挥官和政府领导人也未获此特权。此外，还为调查团准备了专门的办公室，以便他们在南京停留期间拥有开展工作所需的一切便利设施。

军官励志协会的王金林少将（Major-General Wang Jin-lin）在协会大楼入口处亲自欢迎李顿勋爵和马雷斯科蒂伯爵，随后将他们引见给外交部次长徐谟先生（Mr. Hsu Mo）。舒适的接待大厅供调查团使用，此处供应茶水并提供音乐娱乐。

可能前往汉口

徐谟先生在接受路透社采访时称，今天下午或今晚均未安排招待调查团的活动，将给予他们休息的机会。国联调查团成员今晨谈及从南京前往汉口的可能性，但在此方面尚未做出任何明确决定。然而，外交部部分职员正前往汉口，为调查团溯江而上的行程做必要准备。

政府今天下午收到来自宜昌（Yihsin）的电报，称麦考伊将军（General McCoy）、克劳德尔将军（General Claudel）和施尼博士（Dr. Schnee）于下午1时30分启程前往南京，预计于4时30分抵达铜山（Tongshan）。由于他们不在铜山停留，预计他们将在五点到六点之间抵达南京。

李顿勋爵和阿尔德罗万迪·马雷斯科蒂伯爵是顾维钧博士及夫人的午餐客人，用餐地点在铁道部寓所，顾博士及其夫人现住于此。

顾夫人是“太古”轮上的焦点人物，她一在南京登陆，立即被一大群美国摄影师包围。人们为她和她那四只可爱的北京犬拍摄了数百张照片，顾夫人笑着忍受了这一折磨。她迷人的个性迅速使她在各界成为受欢迎的人物。—路透社。

其他成员抵达

3月27日。—麦考伊将军、克劳德尔将军和施尼博士于今晚7时30分抵达南京。—路透社。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, MARCH 27, 1932

Manchurian Tour Is
Commenced Yesterday
By League Commission

Delegates Leave Shanghai In Two Parties; Lord
Lytton And Count Aldrovandi Journey
By River To Nanking

GENERAL CLAUDEL, MAJ.-GEN. MCCOY, AND
DR. SCHNEE, TRAVEL BY TRAIN

Following eleven days, which have been crowded with
receptions, meetings and dinner parties, the League of
Nations Commission of Inquiry left Shanghai yesterday
morning on the first stage of their tour into China and then
on to Manchuria. Of the five delegates who comprise the
party, three left by train for Hangchow, while Lord Lytton
and the Count Luigi Aldrovandi Marescotti, departed for
Nanking by river.

As was pointed out by Lord
Lytton, Chairman of the Commis-
sion at a meeting on Friday night
in the Cathay Hotel, the Shang-
hai and the Manchurian affairs
are viewed by the League of
Nations as separate incidents, and
the data that has been compiled
here on Shanghai question by the
Commission, was only the evidence
that had direct bearing on the
Manchuria subject. At present,
the Commission's main task is
the compilation of memorandum
and evidence on Manchuria, and
following their short stay in
Shanghai, the delegates com-
menced their journey to the
interior yesterday.

Three or four weeks may pass
before the Commission will return
to Shanghai, from where they will
go to Japan. Then they will come
back to China and at some resort
where the hot weather will not
affect them in the great task that
lies ahead, they will deliberate
and come to conclusions before
starting off for Geneva.

However, the date of departure
for Geneva is a long way off,
and yesterday the second step in
the work of completion of the
big undertaking was commenced.
The first step was the taking of
evidence in Shanghai; the second
step was the start of the journey
to Nanking.

Lord Lytton and Count
Aldrovandi left at noon on the
Jardine Matheson river steamer,
Tuckwo. The steamer was boarded
at Hunt's wharf in Hongkew.

General Wu Teh-chen, the
Mayor of Greater Shanghai, and
a party of Chinese dignitaries,
were present to wave farewell to
Lord Lytton, Count Aldrovandi,
and Dr. Wellington Koo, who was
to travel with the members to
Nanking. Dr. Koo was accom-
panied by his wife.

The Second Party

The second party of Commission
delegates had left earlier in the
morning. General Henri Claudel,
Major-General F. Ross McCoy,
and His Excellency Dr. Albert H.
H. Schnee, comprised the first
batch of delegates to leave Shang-
hai. They travelled by train to
Hangchow, leaving Shanghai by
the South Station. On arrival at
Hangchow the party will do some
sight-seeing, after which they will
resume their journey to Nanking
by motor car.

The time of arrival of the two
separate parties in Nanking may
not coincide, but it is expected
that the Commission will be able
to commence its conversations with
the Government to-morrow morn-
ing.

The 11 days that the Commis-
sion spent in Shanghai was a
strenuous time for the members.
Although their time was chiefly
taken up with dinners and teas,
this schedule cannot be said to be
over-pleasant, when it is repeated
day after day. In fact, towards
the end of the Shanghai sojourn,
it was noticed that the Commis-
sion avoided as many public func-
tion as was possible and confined
their attention to the studying of
documentary evidence submitted
by various prominent personages
and patriotic bodies.

Friday's Calls

The Commission was kept busy
to the last moment with these
meetings, for on Friday they re-
ceived a number of people. Dur-
ing the day a number of prominent
Chinese Christians were received,
also representatives of the Chinese
Chamber of Commerce, a group
of Chinese women leaders, Dr.
Wellington Koo, the Relief Society
for Shanghai War Refugees, and
Trade Union leaders.

A delegation of eight members,
representing the Shanghai Gen-
eral Labour Union, called on the
Commission, charging that the
Manchow Kuo state is only a pup-
pet of the Japanese aggression.
The actual figure of jobless work-
ers in this city through the un-
declared war was also reported to
the Commissioners.

The members of the delegation
who met the Commissioners, were
Messrs. Fu Teh-wei, Ha Chin-Shih,
Li Yung-hsiang, Chen Po-teh, Yu
Hsien-ting, Chow Hsieh-siang,
Own Bui-fu and Li Mun-lan.

Later in the day Lord Lytton
received the Press. His Lordship
expressed pleasure at the news
that the peace negotiations were
proceeding smoothly. Lord Lytton
mentioned that one of the chief
thoughts in the minds of Commis-
sion members on landing in
Shanghai, was that a truce be-
tween the two nations should be
consummated. That parleys to that
end were being sponsored by both
sides was pleasing news to him.

《上海星期泰晤士报》，1932年3月27日

国联调查团
昨日启程赴满洲

代表分两批离开上海；李顿勋爵与阿尔德罗万迪伯爵
乘船前往南京

克劳德尔将军、麦考伊少将及
施内博士乘火车前往

在经历了充满招待会、会议和晚宴的十一天后，国际联盟调查团于昨日上午离开上海，开始了他们前往中国内地继而前往满洲的行程的第一阶段。由五名代表组成的调查团中，三人乘火车前往杭州，而李顿勋爵（Lord Lytton）和路易吉·阿尔德罗万迪·马雷斯科蒂伯爵（Count Luigi Aldrovandi Marescotti）则乘船前往南京。

正如调查团主席李顿勋爵在周五晚于华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel）举行的一次会议上所指出的那样，国际联盟将上海事务与满洲事务视为独立的事件，调查团在上海就上海问题汇编的资料，仅是与满洲议题直接相关的证据。目前，调查团的主要任务是编纂关于满洲的备忘录和证据，在短暂停留上海之后，代表们于昨日开始了前往内地的旅程。

调查团可能需要三到四周的时间才会返回上海，随后他们将前往日本。之后他们将回到中国，在一个酷暑不会影响其完成前方重大任务的度假胜地，进行审议并得出结论，然后再启程前往日内瓦。

然而，启程前往日内瓦的日期尚早，昨日，这项庞大工作的完成过程中的第二步已经开始。第一步是在上海取证；第二步是启程前往南京。

李顿勋爵和阿尔德罗万迪伯爵于中午乘坐怡和洋行（Jardine Matheson）的内河轮船“太古”号（Tuckwo）离开。该轮船在虹口亨氏码头（Hunt's wharf）登船。

大上海市市长吴铁城将军以及一批中国显要人物到场，向李顿勋爵、阿尔德罗万迪伯爵以及顾维钧博士挥手送别，顾博士将随同成员们前往南京。顾博士由其夫人陪同。

第二批人员

调查团的第二批代表已于当日早些时候离开。亨利·克劳德尔将军（General Henri Claudel）、F. 罗斯·麦考伊少将（Major-General F. Ross McCoy）和阿尔伯特·H. H. 施内博士阁下（His Excellency Dr. Albert H. H. Schnee）组成了第一批离开上海的代表。他们从上海南站乘火车前往杭州。抵达杭州后，该团将进行一些观光活动，随后将乘汽车继续前往南京。

两批人员抵达南京的时间可能不一致，但预计调查团将于明日上午开始与中国政府进行会谈。

调查团在上海度过的11天对成员们来说是一段紧张的时期。虽然他们的时间主要花在晚宴和茶会上，但这种日程日复一日地重复，很难说是令人愉快的。事实上，在上海逗留接近尾声时，人们注意到调查团尽可能避免参加公共活动，而将注意力集中在研究各界知名人士和爱国团体提交的书面证据上。

周五的拜访

调查团直到最后一刻都忙于这些会议，因为他们在周五接待了许多人。白天，他们接待了一批著名的中国基督徒、中国总商会的代表、一批中国女性领袖、顾维钧博士、上海战难民救济社以及工会领袖。

一个由八名成员组成的代表团，代表上海总工会，拜访了调查团，指控伪满洲国仅仅是日本侵略的傀儡。由于这场未宣战的战争，本市失业工人的实际人数也向委员们作了报告。

会见委员的代表团成员包括：傅德伟（Fu Teh-wei，音译）、哈金世（Ha Chin-Shih，音译）、李永祥（Li Yung-hsiang，音译）、陈伯德（Chen Po-teh，音译）、余贤定（Yu Hsien-ting，音译）、周协相（Chow Hsieh-siang，音译）、Own Bui-fu（原文不清/音译）和李木兰（Li Mun-lan，音译）。

当天晚些时候，李顿勋爵接见了新闻界。勋爵对和平谈判顺利进行的消息表示高兴。李顿勋爵提到，调查团成员抵达上海时的主要想法之一，就是两国之间应达成停战协议。得知双方都在为此进行洽谈，令他感到欣慰。

The League Commission
NANKING, Mar. 25.—The Ministry for Foreign Affairs this morning received a report from Shanghai that three members of the League Commission, four Japanese and several of the staff of the Commission, accompanied by Mr. Chang and others are leaving to-morrow morning for Hangchow, en route to Nanking.

The Foreign Ministry has dispatched ten motor cars to Hangchow for the use of the Commission and public organizations in Nanking are making feverish preparations for their welcome here. Placards are already to be seen on the streets bearing inscriptions of welcome and such messages as “anti-Japanese militarism not anti-foreign” and “Give us justice.”—Reuter.

Arrangements In Nanking
NANKING, Mar. 26.—Preparations are complete for the reception of the League Commission, some members of which are expected to arrive here to-morrow at noon. The period of their stay in Nanking is tentatively set at four days and the programme planned, therefore, has been fixed as follows:—
March 28: Morning, calling on Government Leaders; Noon, Mr. Wang Chi-wei’s luncheon at the Railway Ministry; Evening, Dr. Lo Wen-kan’s dinner at the Overseas Chinese building.
March 29: Morning, interview with Chairman of National Government, Mr. Lin Sen; Evening, dinner given by Mr. Lin Sen.
March 30: Evening, dinner given by General Chiang Kai-shek at Officers’ Moral Endeavour association.
March 31: Morning, sightseeing; Noon, tiffin by members of the C.E.C. at the Sun Yat-sen Memorial Park.

Adopted Regulations
As a result of repeated discussions between Central Party headquarters, the Executive Yuan, the Foreign Office, the Municipal Kuomintang office and police and military organizations, regulations have been adopted governing the reception of the League commissioners.
When the commissioners arrive at the Hsiakwan wharf one representative each of the Foreign Office, Nanking Municipal Government, and War and Navy ministries, will meet them. When the commissioners leave the boat the Navy Ministry band is to furnish music of welcome. All motor cars required will be furnished by the Foreign Office, and all cars will bear special signs, without which no car will be allowed to proceed to Hsiakwang at the time of the Commission’s arrival.
People in groups are permitted to stand on the sides of street to welcome the Commission but are not permitted to have bands or to shout slogans or distribute printed matter.

When the American, German and French commissioners come to Nanking from Hangchow, they will be received by four representatives of the National Government with a band playing at the entrance to the Moral Endeavour Association.—Reuter.

Precautions At Nanking
NANKING, March 26.—Special precautionary measures are being taken to prevent disorderly scenes at Hsiakwan wharf when Lord Lytton and the other League commissioners accompanying him arrive to-morrow morning. People welcoming the commissioners, who are expected to arrive at 11 o’clock, will only be permitted to wait at designated positions along the Chunshan Road, along which traffic will be stopped.

Only four authorised representatives are to meet the commissioners; only those with special badges will be allowed to wait at the wharf. The four representatives will include General Ku Chen-lun, acting Mayor of Nanking, General Chen Yi, Vice-Minister of War, Mr. Hsu Mo, Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs, and possibly Dr. Lo Wen-kan, the Minister for Foreign Affairs.

Special Guards
Special guards will be stationed along the Chunshan Road from the wharf to the Officers’ Moral Endeavour Association where they will stay. Press correspondents have been requested not to seek interviews when the commissioners arrive, but to await them at the Officers’ Moral Endeavour Association, where the flags of all nations are already flying.

Elaborate preparations have been made to assure the commissioners all possible comfort and convenience.

Beginning from to-day people without special badges will not be allowed to enter the buildings of the Association.

The Japanese assessors will stay at the local Japanese consulate.—Reuter.

Hangchow Party
NANKING, Mar. 26.—The Foreign Office has received a telegram stating that General McCoy and other members of the League Commission who went to Hangchow are leaving that city to-morrow for Nanking.

They are expected to arrive at Yihsin at noon. The Foreign Office has sent Mr. Woo Lan-ju, chief of the International Affairs Department, to Yihsin to await their arrival. The delegates will leave Yihsin for Nanking to-morrow afternoon.—Reuter.

国联调查团
南京，3月25日电。—外交部今晨收到来自上海的报告称，国联调查团的三名成员、四名日本人以及调查团的几名工作人员，在张先生等人陪同下，将于明晨离开上海前往杭州，途中转往南京。

外交部已派遣十辆汽车前往杭州供调查团使用，南京的公共组织正在狂热地准备在此欢迎他们。街道上已经可以看到写有欢迎辞以及“反对日本军国主义而非反对外国人”、“给我们正义”等标语的告示牌。—路透社。

南京的安排
南京，3月26日电。—迎接国联调查团的准备工作已全部就绪，部分成员预计将于明日中午抵达此处。他们在南京的停留时间暂定为四天，因此制定的计划如下：—
3月28日：上午，拜会政府领导人；中午，汪精卫先生在铁道部的午餐；晚上，罗文干博士在海外大厦举行的晚宴。
3月29日：上午，会见国民政府主席林森先生；晚上，林森先生举行的晚宴。
3月30日：晚上，蒋介石将军在军官励志社举行的晚宴。
3月31日：上午，观光；中午，中央执行委员会成员在中山纪念公园举行的便餐。

通过的规章
经过中央党部、行政院、外交部、市国民党党部以及警军机构的反复讨论，已通过管辖接待国联专员的规章。
当专员们抵达下关码头时，外交部、南京市政府以及陆军部和海军部将各派一名代表迎接。当专员们离船时，海军部乐队将奏乐欢迎。所需的所有汽车均由外交部提供，所有车辆均须悬挂特殊标志，无此标志的车辆在调查团抵达期间不得前往下关。
允许成群结队的人站在街道两侧欢迎调查团，但不允许携带乐队、高呼口号或分发印刷品。

当美国、德国和法国专员从杭州来到南京时，将由国民政府的四名代表在励志社入口处奏乐迎接。—路透社。

南京的预防措施
南京，3月26日电。—为防止李顿勋爵及其他随行的国联专员明晨抵达时下关码头出现混乱场面，正在采取特别的预防措施。预计专员们将于11点抵达，欢迎的人群只允许在中山路沿线的指定位置等候，该路段的交通将被阻断。

只有四名授权代表可以迎接专员；只有佩戴特殊徽章的人才允许在码头等候。这四名代表包括南京代市长谷正伦将军、陆军次长陈仪将军、外交部次长徐谟先生，以及可能的外交部长罗文干博士。

特别警卫

从码头到专员们将下榻的军官励志社，中山路沿线将部署特别警卫。已要求新闻记者在专员抵达时不要寻求采访，而是在军官励志社等候，那里已经悬挂着各国国旗。

为确保专员们获得尽可能多的舒适和便利，已做了详尽的准备。

从今天起，没有特殊徽章的人不得进入励志社大楼。

日本顾问将住在当地的日本领事馆。—路透社。

杭州一行
南京，3月26日电。—外交部收到电报称，前往杭州的国联调查团成员麦考伊将军等人将于明日离开该市前往南京。

预计他们将于中午抵达宜兴。外交部已派遣国际司司长吴兰茹先生前往宜兴等候他们的到来。代表们将于明日下午离开宜兴前往南京。—路透社。

THE NORTH-CHINA SUNDAY NEWS, MARCH 27, 1932

DEPARTURE OF MISSION

League Investigators Leave Shanghai:
Big Reception at Nanking

Concluding their stay in Shang-hai for purposes of an investigation of the Sino-Japanese dispute the members of the League of Nations Commission of Inquiry left yesterday morning, some of the party for Nanking and others for Hang-chow.

On the I.C.S.N. Tuckwo at noon yesterday there departed for Nan-king Lord Lytton, Chairman of the Commission, Count Marescotti of Italy and several members of the Commission's staff. Early in the forenoon General Claudel of France, Dr. H. H. Schnee of Ger-many, General F. R. McCoy of America and members of the staff left for Hangchow from Shanghai South station.

Accompanying the Commission members to Nanking on the Tuckwo are Dr. Wellington Koo and Mr. I. Yoshida, respectively Assessors for China and Japan to the Commis-sion. Also travelling on the ship are Dr. Pelt, Assistant Secretary to the Commission, Dr. Liegois, Messrs. Pastukov, Charrere and D. Roberts. With the Hangchow party are Dr. Goullet, Professor Blakeloo, Dr. Young, Messrs. Biddle, von Klotze and Pepin.

Mr. Haas, Secretary General to the Commission, and Mr. W. W. Astor are going direct to Nanking by air from Shanghai instead of accompanying either party. The Hangchow party is to proceed to Nanking by road.

Valuable Information

Interviewed yesterday by the "North-China Daily News," Lord Lytton stated that the Commis-sion's visit to Shanghai had been of great value. A large amount of first-hand information had been acquired as regards the "Shanghai Incident" and a number of wit-nesses had given important testi-mony to members of the Commis-sion.

Lord Lytton stated that the mem-bers of the Commission had had very little time to themselves in Shanghai, and that dinner and tiffin engagements had had the effect of crowding up their other work. They had, however, learn-ed a lot through their stay in Shanghai, short though it was.

After visiting Nanking the Com-mission is going to the north, either direct or by way of Hankow, al-though whether the latter port will be visited or not has not as yet been decided, for its Man-churian investigation.

Before returning to Europe, which they expect to reach in August, the members of the Com-mission will visit Nanking once more, as well as Japan. Lord Lytton yesterday stated that before they go back some place will have to be found for a conference, but he does not consider it likely that the Commission will revisit Shang-hai.

There was quite a fair number of people on board the Tuckwo yesterday saying farewell or "au revoir" to the Commission, but there was nothing in the way of an organised send-off or demonstration at the wharf.

Nanking Programme

Nanking, Mar. 26.

The following programme for the reception of the League Commission of Enquiry, which is due to arrive here from Shanghai to-morrow, has been announced by the special reception committee of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs:-

Monday, March 28:-
Calls upon leading officials in the morning.
Tiffin by Mr. Wang Ching-wei, Pre-sident of the Executive Yuan.
Dinner by Mr. Lo Wen-kan, Minister of Foreign Affairs.

Tuesday, 29:-
Interviews with leading officials.
Audience with President Lin Sen.
Dinner by President Lin Sen at the National Government building.

Wednesday, 30:-
Dinner by General Chiang Kai-shek, President of the Military Affairs Commission.

Thursday, 31:-
Visit to historic and scenic spots in the morning.
Tiffin by C.E.C. members at the Mausoleum Gardens.

The Commission will be greeted upon arrival at Hsiakwan by dele-gates from the Ministries of For-eign Affairs, War, and the Navy and the Nanking Municipality.

Representatives of various peo-ple's organisations will line the road from the Hsiakwan wharf to the Officers' Moral Endeavor Society to welcome the Commission.-Kuo Min.

Nanking, Mar. 25.

The Ministry for Foreign Affairs this morning received a report from Shanghai that three members of the League Commission, four Japanese and several of the staff of the Com-mission, accompanied by Mr. Chang and others are leaving to-morrow morning for Hangchow, en route to Nanking.

The Foreign Ministry has de-spatched ten motor-cars to Hang-chow for the use of the Commission and public organisations in Nan-king are making feverish prepara-tions for the welcome.

Placards are already to be seen on the streets bearing inscriptions of welcome and such messages as "anti-Japanese militarism not anti-foreign" and "Give us justice".-Reuter.

《华北星期日报》，1932年3月27日

调查团离沪

国联调查员离开上海：
南京举行盛大欢迎仪式

为调查中日争端而在上海停留的国联调查委员会成员于昨晨离去，部分人员前往南京，其余人员前往杭州。

昨午，调查团主席李顿勋爵（Lord Lytton）、意大利代表马雷斯科蒂伯爵（Count Marescotti）及调查团数名职员乘坐工部局巡船“大沽”号（I.C.S.N. Tuckwo）启程前往南京。上午早些时候，法国代表克劳德尔将军（General Claudel）、德国代表施内博士（Dr. H. H. Schnee）、美国代表麦考伊少将（General F. R. McCoy）及职员从上海南站出发前往杭州。

随同调查团成员乘“大沽”号前往南京的还有分别担任调查团中方和日方顾问的顾维钧博士（Dr. Wellington Koo）和吉田伊三郎先生（Mr. I. Yoshida）。同船同行的还有调查团助理秘书佩尔特博士（Dr. Pelt）、利热瓦博士（Dr. Liegois）、帕斯图科夫先生（Messrs. Pastukov）、夏雷尔先生（Charrere）和D·罗伯茨先生（D. Roberts）。随同前往杭州的一行人员包括古莱博士（Dr. Goullet）、布莱克卢教授（Professor Blakeloo）、杨博士（Dr. Young）、比德尔先生（Messrs. Biddle）、冯·克洛策先生（von Klotze）和佩潘先生（Pepin）。

调查团秘书长哈斯先生（Mr. Haas）和W·W·阿斯特先生（Mr. W. W. Astor）将直接从上海乘飞机前往南京，而不随同任何一组人员行动。杭州组将经陆路前往南京。

宝贵的情报

李顿勋爵昨日接受《字林西报》采访时称，调查团对上海的访问极具价值。关于“上海事变”，调查团获得了大量第一手资料，许多证人向调查团成员提供了重要证词。

李顿勋爵表示，调查团成员在上海几乎没有自己的时间，晚宴和午餐会等活动挤占了他们的其他工作。然而，尽管停留时间短暂，他们在上海期间仍获益良多。

在访问南京后，调查团将北上进行满洲调查，路线可能是直达，也可能经由汉口，但是否访问汉口这一港口城市尚未决定。

在预计于八月返回欧洲之前，调查团成员将再次访问南京以及日本。李顿勋爵昨日表示，在他们回去之前，必须找一个地方召开会议，但他认为调查团不太可能重访上海。

昨日，“大沽”号上有相当多的人向调查团道别或说“再见”，但码头并未组织任何形式的送行或示威活动。

南京行程安排

南京，3月26日电。

外交部特别接待委员会公布了以下接待国联调查团的日程安排，该调查团预计将于明日从上海抵达此处：

3月28日，星期一：
上午拜会主要官员。
行政院院长汪精卫先生设午宴。
外交部长罗文干先生设晚宴。

29日，星期二：
会见主要官员。
谒见林森主席。
林森主席在国民政府大楼设晚宴。

30日，星期三：
军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军设晚宴。

31日，星期四：
上午参观名胜古迹。
中央执行委员会成员在陵园花园设午宴。

调查团抵达下关时，将受到外交部、军政部、海军部及南京市代表的迎接。

各界民众团体代表将在从下关码头到励志社的道路上列队欢迎调查团。——《国民新闻》

南京，3月25日电。

外交部今晨收到上海报告称，国联调查团三名成员、四名日本人及调查团数名职员，由张先生等人陪同，将于明晨启程前往杭州，途中转往南京。

外交部已派遣十辆汽车前往杭州供调查团使用，南京的各公共组织正热烈准备欢迎事宜。

街头已可见到写有欢迎标语的宣传牌，以及“反对日本军国主义而非反对外国人”、“还我公道”等口号。——路透社

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, MARCH 25, 1932

THE LEAGUE MISSION

Members Surprised At Alleged Chinese
Dissatisfaction With Labours

Declaring their complete surprise at the protest reported to have been cabled to the League of Nations at Geneva by Mr. T. V. Soong, the Chinese Minister of Finance, the members of the International Commission of Inquiry, now in Shanghai, last evening professed entire inability to understand or explain the alleged dissatisfaction with the activities of the Mission here.

"All arrangements relative to our reception here and the activities of the Commission in Shanghai were prepared in close collaboration with Dr. Wellington Koo, the Assessor appointed to the Mission by the Chinese Government, and other Chinese officials," the spokesman for the International body declared last evening. "At no time has any dissatisfaction on the part of the Chinese Government been indicated to us, until we were advised of this message."

In fact, previous to yesterday it was known that the members of the Mission had been urged to prolong their stay in Shanghai by several days at least, additional Chinese organisations being desirous of extending hospitality or arranging meetings with the delegation.

The protest will not affect in any way the future plans of the Commission, it was stated last night, all arrangements having been completed for the departure of the delegates for Nanking on Saturday morning.

Minister's Statement

In relation to the incident, Mr. Quo Tai-chi, the Chinese Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs, last night issued the following statement:

"This morning's press reports about a Chinese protest to the League over the delay of the Commission of Inquiry in proceeding to Manchuria caused much surprise in Chinese quarters.

"No instructions were sent to Dr. W. W. Yen to protest about the attitude of the Commission on any subject, still less about their welcome sojourn in Shanghai. An inquiry has been addressed to the Chinese delegate by telegraph in order to ascertain the accuracy of the press reports from Geneva.

"Our anxiety about the rapid developments in Manchuria, rendering the situation more complicated every day, is a well-known fact, and the Chinese delegate has been constantly kept informed of these developments and our views. If any communication of the reported tenor was addressed to the League on the subject, it must have been entirely due to an error in telegraphic transmission.

"There could not be any grounds for dissatisfaction on the part of the Chinese side, as there was none in fact because the programme of the Commission was arranged in full consultation with the Chinese representative."

Visitors Received

The morning yesterday again was devoted by the Commission to receiving visitors in conference relative to the subject of its investigation. The afternoon yesterday was devoted to study of the minutes of the various conferences previously held in this city, and the perusal of submitted documents.

While changes yet may be made in the personnel of the two parties, in which the Commission will divide to-morrow on its departure from Shanghai, it is believed that General Henri Claudel, the French Delegate, and Major-General Frank Ross McCoy, the American member, will leave by train for Hangchow, and thence to Nanking by motor car. The Earl of Lytton and Count Luigi Aldrovandi Marescotti, the Italian Delegate, will embark direct for the National Capital on board the I-C.N.S. Tuckwo. together with a number of the attaches and secretaries. Dr. Hermann Heinrich Schnee had not decided last night which route he would take.

国联调查团

成员对中国据称不满其工作表示惊讶

国际调查委员会目前在上海的成员昨晚表示，对于据称由中国财政部长宋子文先生向日内瓦国联发出的抗议电报感到完全惊讶，并声称完全无法理解或解释据称对调查团在此地活动的不满。

该国际机构的发言人昨晚宣称：“关于我们在此地的接待以及调查团在上海的活动的所有安排，都是与由中国政府指派为调查团顾问的顾维钧博士及其他中国官员密切合作准备的。在得知此消息之前，中国政府从未向我们表示过任何不满。”

事实上，在昨天之前，众所周知，调查团成员曾被敦促至少在上海多停留几天，因为更多的中国组织希望款待代表团或安排与代表团会面。

昨晚有人表示，抗议不会影响调查团未来的计划，所有代表于周六上午启程前往南京的安排均已就绪。

部长的声明

针对此事，中国外交部次长郭泰祺先生昨晚发表如下声明：

“今晨有关中国就调查团推迟前往满洲一事向国联提出抗议的新闻报道，在中国方面引起了极大惊讶。

“并未指示颜惠庆博士（Dr. W. W. Yen）就调查团在任何问题上的态度提出抗议，更未就其在上海受到的热情招待提出抗议。已通过电报向中国代表查询，以核实来自日内瓦的新闻报道的准确性。

“我们对满洲局势迅速变化、致使情况日益复杂化的担忧是众所周知的事实，中国代表不断获知这些进展及我们的观点。如果确实发出了具有上述报道语气的致国联通函，那必定完全是由于电报传输错误所致。

“中方没有任何不满的理由，因为事实上并不存在不满，调查团的日程安排是与中方代表充分协商后制定的。”

接待访客

昨天上午，调查团再次用于接待访客，就其调查主题进行会谈。昨天下午则用于研究此前在本市举行的各次会议的记录，并审阅提交的文档。

虽然调查团明天离开上海时分成的两组人员构成可能还会有变动，但据信，法国代表亨利·克劳德尔将军（General Henri Claudel）和美国成员弗兰克·罗斯·麦考伊少将（Major-General Frank Ross McCoy）将乘火车前往杭州，然后乘汽车前往南京。李顿伯爵和意大利代表路易吉·阿尔多万迪·马雷斯科蒂伯爵（Count Luigi Aldrovandi Marescotti）将与多名随员和秘书一起，直接乘坐工部局巡船“大沽”号（I-C.N.S. Tuckwo）前往首都。赫尔曼·海因里希·施内博士（Dr. Hermann Heinrich Schnee）昨晚尚未决定采取哪条路线。

Letters To The Editor

Communications intended for publication in this column
must be accompanied by the name and address of the sender,
as a guarantee of good faith.

CHINA AND JAPAN
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—I send you herewith copy
of a letter I addressed to a local
weekly which remained unpublish-
ed. Certain extracts were however
commented upon in which I am
taken strongly to task—a pro-
cedure that pleases me immensely
as it signifies that some of my
statements “got home.”
I hardly think that I am
damning everything and every-
body as the commentary states. In
a question as involved as the
Sino-Japanese conflict is, it is un-
just to attribute entire blame to
Japan for her “aggression” as the
journal does, nor alone to her op-
ponent, China. The matter goes
far deeper than that of a mere
passage at arms between the two
countries. Every effect has its
cause and if I am a staunch sup-
porter of Japan’s display of force
(against force by the way) it is
because I can see no other method
which would have made the Chin-
ese governing and military cliques
understand that they have been
for a considerable time overstep-
ping the mark of good relations
with Japan and other countries.
Most foreigners strongly wish to
see China attain full sovereignty
and her proper place in the Com-
ity of Nations. But it is not in the
creation of rabble armies, amount-
ing in the aggregate to well over
a million men, which rend the
country to pieces at the behest of
bandit warlords and politicians
that salvation lies; neither in the
draining of the country of its life-
blood and riches for the benefit of
those temporarily in authority—
(because of “squeeze” railways
and steamship lines are left to go
to pieces injuring China’s internal
trade and ruining her credit
abroad; dykes are left unrepaired
causing stupendous loss in life an
property); nor by the fostering,
by those in power, of an insensate
anti-foreignism to cover up their
misdeeds.
My commentator may or may not
be right when he says that I am
“a man in the street” he honours
me highly. He also calls me an
“amateur diplomat.” Thank
Heaven for that! I am sorely
afraid he might have used the
appellation without any qualifica-
tive. He says that I am not
prolific with suggestions as
regards what is to be done. It
is not, in my estimation, so much
a question of what has been done
to China as what has been left
undone. I fully believe that more
co-operation between the Powers
in insisting upon China toeing the
line, and helping her to do so, that
conditions will better themselves.
Weakness is utterly useless and
thinking Chinese, we know, are
strongly of that opinion. If again,

as my critic says, the Diplomats
of the various Powers have tried
for years and failed to pacify or
benefit China (which is distinctly
a black mark against the Diplom-
ats!) why not let Japan alone do
the work? She knows the Chinese
much better than other foreign-
ers do and will achieve success
where others have failed. I am a
strong supporter of Japanese
action in Manchuria because I
know (having lived in those
parts) that Japan has brought
and is still further going to bring
peace and economic contentment
to millions of Chinese who have
settled there. If she does benefit
from her move, what Nation is
there to cast stones at her?
P. H. D.
Shanghai, March 24, 1932.
[Copy]
Sir.—The airy manner in which you
appear to pass judgment on Japan’s
actions here is good. To attribute to
her the entire blame for a situation
the fundamental cause of which lies
not alone in the acts of “aggression”
of which both contestants have so far
adjudged each other guilty—with
consequent enmity between them—
but in the Policy which the various
Powers, with interests in China, have
been pursuing for many years past, is
hardly fair.
As regards the destruction of
Chapei there is no, and cannot be,
any difficulty in proving that the
Chinese Troops deliberately fired the
entire section which they occupied
previous to beating a hasty retreat.
I am not so much pro-Japanese or
anti-Chinese as I am pro-Law, Order
and Good Government; and if it be a
matter of choosing between that and
what we have been pleased to call the
Chinese Government, give me Law
and Order. And the Japanese variety
is as good, if not even better, than
any other. And now we have the
League of Nations, fresh from the
mess it made of the Manchurian
Question at Geneva, trying to solve
differences between two Eastern
nations according to Western Stand-
ards. It can’t be done Sir, and the
less the League interferes the better
the prospects of an early Peace. If
the Kellogg Pact and the Nine-Power
Treaty are to be held applicable to
Japan they are no less applicable to
China. There is only this difference
—Japan is a Selling nation and China
a Buying one and the spoken sympa-
thies of those against whom Japan
competes with so much success must
of necessity veer towards the second.
This is only human. That is what
explains the practically total con-
demnation by the British and Ameri-
can Press of Japan. As if Editors
EXPRESSED Public Opinion!! Most
emphatically they do not. They say
just what they are told to by the
men behind the scene; they do try
however to MAKE Public Opinion
which is hardly the same.
And those self-same influences are
working to-day insofar as the in-
dividual Members of the League
Commission and the American Re-
presentative are concerned. Each one,
whilst acting as judge or arbiter,
must needs be guided by the Policy to
which his Government subscribes. In
other words, self-interest will
dominate here just as it has dominat-
ed elsewhere. Listen to what the
Washington correspondent to the

致编辑的信

凡拟在本栏刊登的来信，必须附有寄信人的姓名和地址，以资诚信。

中国与日本
编辑先生，
《上海泰晤士报》
先生，——兹附上我此前投给本地一家周刊但未被刊登的一封信的副本。然而，该刊对信中的某些摘录进行了评论，并在评论中对我大加挞伐——这一程序令我甚感欣慰，因为它意味着我的一些陈述“切中要害”。
我 hardly 认为像评论所说的那样，我在诅咒一切人和事。在中日冲突如此错综复杂的问题上，像该刊物那样将全部罪责归咎于日本的“侵略”，或者单独归咎于其对手中国，都是不公正的。此事远比两国之间单纯的武力冲突要深刻得多。凡事必有因，如果我坚决支持日本展示武力（顺带说一句，是以武力对抗武力），那是因为我看不出还有其他方法能让中国的执政集团和军事派系明白，他们在相当长的一段时间里已经越过了与日本及其他国家保持良好关系的界限。
大多数外国人强烈希望看到中国获得完全的主权，并在国际社会中享有其应有的地位。但是，救赎之道并不在于建立那些总计超过百万人的乌合之众军队，这些军队在匪帮军阀和政客的指使下将国家撕得粉碎；也不在于为了暂时掌权者的利益而榨干国家的血汗和财富——（由于“勒索”，铁路和轮船公司任其破败，损害了中国的国内贸易并破坏了其在海外的信用；堤防失修，导致生命财产的巨大损失）；更不在于当权者煽动盲目的排外情绪以掩盖其恶行。
我的评论员说我是一个“普通人”，无论他说得对错，他都极大地抬举了我。他还称我为“业余外交家”。谢天谢地！我非常担心他可能会不加任何修饰地使用这个称呼。他说我在建议该做什么方面并不高产。在我看来，问题不在于对中国做了什么，而在于没做什么。我完全相信，如果列强在坚持要求中国守规矩并帮助其做到这一点方面加强合作，局势将会好转。软弱是毫无用处的，我们知道，有思想的中国人也强烈持有这种观点。如果再次，

pages.en:
Lady Pontifical of the Bund has to
say on the subject of the League of
Nations—"It had strayed far from
the path mapped out for it and had
become a mere European Club where
selfish nations intrigued against one
another and manoeuvred for
advantage"!!!! Brutally frank? Yes.
True? Answer the question yourself.
The very nations whose whole
history is but a series of acts of
"aggression" are going to sit in
judgment over Japan's default!
Threats to flay her alive (I exag-
gerate to make the point) are bandied
about in private letters which are
immediately cabled to every capital
of the world to indicate how very
private they are) because she has
not maintained peace And the most
Peace-less Nation, or more correctly,
Country, within the last two decades
has been China!!! Countless mas-
sacres of the people in their millions;
banditry run completely wild; yet not
a word is said, nothing done to help.
A Pawn in the game of the Inter-
national Scramble for Trade (as if
that was the only thing worth while
in this world), China has been
pandered to in a manner which has
led to her undoing and her present
discomfiture. Every fault of hers has
been condoned, every act of aggres-
sion calmly submitted to. Treaties,
solemn agreements, promises, she has
been allowed to flout them all. Pro-
ceeding one step further in an illegal
attempt to throttle Japanese trade,
she finds herself face to face with
an opponent who will brook no fur-
ther nonsense, she now writhes in
helplessness and anger. I do not
blame her so much as those who caus-
ed her to take that very unfortunate
road. The ruins of Chapei and
Kiangwan do not make me reflect too
much upon the futility of War as
upon the utter insincerity and total
bankruptcy of International Diplo-
macy as dictated by the worshippers
of Mammon. For a considerable time
now this Divinity and Mars have
walked hand in hand; in fact, it is
hard to distinguish which is which.
The partnership has brought the
World to its present parlous condi-
tions. And we continue to blather
about PEACE!! By all means let us
thrust Peace if we can upon Japan;
but by the same token let there be
Peace in China and throughout the
world. Aggression after all has
other characters than the purely
military one—and from Capitalistic
Aggression as well may the Lord
deliver us and all Nations!
We hear very much these days of
plans and schemes; innumerable and
grandiose for the welfare of future
Shanghai. I have read about and
listened to most of them and the
dominant note throughout is again
"self-interest." So long as we are
able to make capital out of the Chin-
ese what does it matter how the
Chinese people as a whole fare!

The greater the troubles in China
the merrier so long as the process of
self-destruction does not carry to
total extinction as that would be bad
for then there would be nobody left
upon whom to foist our goods!
There is going to be no solution
to the Chinese Question (as affect-
ing Shanghai and other foreign
entities in China) of any real and
lasting benefit which does not take
into account the bettering of condi-
tions throughout that unfortunate
land. The future of Shanghai is in-
extricably bound to the future of
China. If all the Powers, with
interests here, could only sink their
petty differences and really and
sincerely desire China's good they
can help her, without very much
difficulty, in attaining Peace and a
fairly good government. The same
rules practically apply here as do in
the West. The medicine no doubt
would be a little bitter at first—for
China and for everybody concerned—
but the cure would justify its
ministering. Facts however must be
frankly faced even if unpleasant and
the first of these is that a Chinese
Government, representative of the
country and its people, does NOT
exist. If certain Powers will con-
tinue their ridiculous attitude of
recognising by various acts a mere
group of men, out for their own
ends and professing a power which
they do not really possess, and go
to the extent of even making Treaties
with such men, the very same trouble
as occurred recently will occur again
at no distant date but in a very much
worse form. It Extraterritoriality
is to continue let it be maintained in
fact and not only in name. If it is
out-of-date and must be replaced, the
sooner this is done the better. But
whatever the form of relationship
with China that is ultimately adopted
it must be one that takes into con-
sideration the actual state of affairs
in the country, not forgetting the
very peculiar psychology of its people
—and the Pact must be strictly ad-
hered to both in the letter and in the
spirit by China and the other signato-
ries. And international jealousies
must cease as much as human frailty
will allow.
A fervid anti-militarist at heart,
I much prefer an honest and clear
cut display of force to hypocritical
and secret diplomacy. And so do
you but perhaps it is difficult for you
to say so.
Yours faithfully,
P. H. B.

外滩那位“教皇夫人”（Lady Pontifical）关于国联的说法吧——“它已偏离为其规划的轨道，变成了一个纯粹的欧洲俱乐部，自私的国家在那里相互阴谋诡计，谋取优势”！！！！坦率得残酷？是的。真实吗？请你自己回答这个问题。
正是那些整个历史只是一系列“侵略”行为的国家，将要坐堂审判日本的过失！私下信件中流传着要将她活剥皮的威胁（我夸大其词以说明观点），这些信件随即被电传至世界各国的首都，以表明它们是多么私密），因为她没有维持和平。而在过去二十年里，最缺乏和平的国家，或者更准确地说，最不和平的国家，一直是中国！！！无数民众遭到屠杀，人数以百万计；匪患完全失控；然而却无人置喙，无人施以援手。
作为国际贸易争夺战（仿佛这是世界上唯一值得做的事情）中的一枚棋子，中国受到了一种导致其毁灭和当前困境的纵容。她的每一个过错都被宽恕，每一次侵略行为都被冷静地忍受。条约、庄严协议、承诺，她被允许蔑视这一切。在非法企图扼杀日本贸易的道路上再进一步后，她发现自己面对的是一个不再容忍进一步胡闹的对手，她现在在无助和愤怒中挣扎。我不怎么责怪她，而是责怪那些导致她走上这条非常不幸道路的人。闸北和江湾的废墟并没有让我过多反思战争的徒劳，而是让我反思由金钱崇拜者主导的国际外交的彻底虚伪和完全破产。在相当长的一段时间里，这位财神爷和战神一直携手同行；事实上，很难区分谁是谁。这种伙伴关系将世界带到了目前的危险境地。而我们还在喋喋不休地谈论和平！！无论如何，让我们尽可能将和平强加给日本；但同样地，让中国乃至全世界都实现和平。毕竟，“侵略”还有其他特征，不仅仅是军事性的——愿主保佑我们和所有国家免受资本主义侵略之苦！
这些天我们听到了很多关于未来上海福利的计划和方案；数量众多且宏大。我阅读并聆听了其中的大多数，贯穿始终的主旋律又是“私利”。只要我们能从中国人身上获利，中国人民整体的境遇如何又有什么关系！
中国的麻烦越大越好，只要自我毁灭的过程不至于导致彻底灭绝，因为那将是糟糕的，那样就没有人可以强行推销我们的商品了！
如果不考虑改善那个不幸之地的整体状况，就不会有任何真正和持久有益的解决方案来解决中国问题（就影响上海和其他在华外国实体而言）。上海的未来与中国的未来密不可分。如果所有在此拥有利益的列强能够放下细微的分歧，真诚地希望中国好，他们可以毫不费力地帮助中国实现和平和一个相当不错的政府。同样的规则实际上也适用于西方。这剂药对中国和所有相关方来说起初无疑会有些苦，但疗效将证明其施用的正当性。然而，即使令人不快，也必须坦诚面对事实，其中首要的事实是，一个代表该国及其人民的中国政府并不存在。如果某些列强继续其荒谬的态度，通过各种行为承认一群仅仅为了自身目的、声称拥有其实并不拥有的权力的人，甚至达到与这些人签订条约的程度，那么最近发生的同样的麻烦将在不久的将来再次发生，而且形式会更加恶劣。如果治外法权要继续存在，就让它在事实上而不仅仅是在名义上得到维持。如果它已过时且必须被取代，那么越早这样做越好。但是，无论最终采取何种对华关系形式，都必须考虑到该国的实际状况，不要忘记其人民非常独特的心理——并且中国和其他签署国必须严格在字面上和精神上遵守公约。国际嫉妒必须在人类弱点允许的范围内尽可能停止。
我内心深处是一个热烈的反军国主义者，我更喜欢诚实和明确的武力展示，而不是虚伪和秘密的外交。你也一样，但也许你很难这么说。
此致，
敬礼，
P. H. B.
