Chinese journals belonging to the
Chinese Press Association are the
"Shun Pao", "Sin Wan Pao",
"Eastern Times", "China Times"
and "China Press".

Dinner At Night
Last night Dr. Wellington Koo
invited the members of the
League of Nations Commission
to a dinner party, at 129 Seymour
Road, and in his speech of wel-
come, Dr. Koo said:--
"Lord Lytton and other honour-
able members of the Commission
of Inquiry, and gentlemen:--It
is my pleasant duty as Chinese
Assessor to bid you one and all
a most cordial welcome to China.
Though some of you gentlemen,
perhaps, are visiting the Far
East for the first time, we, how-
ever, feel we have known you all
through the distinguished careers
you have respectively pursued, as
statesman, soldier, or diplomat.
Eminent leaders to undertake the
League most sincerely upon hav-
ing secured such a body of
eminent leaders to undertake the
mission of inquiry into the Sino-
Japanese conflict which has re-
cently aroused the attention of
the whole world. You are wel-
comed to China because you are
apostles of peace and justice.
Under present conditions in China,
the nature of the hospitality that
we can offer must necessarily be
humble and simple nevertheless,
it is both warm and sincere.
"Our welcome is warm and
sincere because you have come
from the League of Nations. The
principles of peace upon which
the League is founded are the
principles most cherished in our
history and literature. Chinese
sages for centuries have taught
us that "the pen is mightier than
the sword." Confucius said that
"within the four seas all men are
brothers." The spirit of the
League, it may be said, is the
spirit of Chinese civilization. It
is for this reason that China was
among the first nations to approve
of the establishment of the
League and it was my happy lot
as Chinese delegate, first to take
part in the work of the Com-
mittee to prepare a draft of the
Covenant under the distinguished
Chairmanship of President Wil-
son, and later to sit on the Coun-
cil and the Assembly during the
first years of its existence."
"Complexity Of Our Problems"
"Since your arrival at this
threshold of China" added Dr.
Koo, "you, gentlemen, may have
already noted that there is move-
ment and life everywhere around
you. As you travel farther and
see more, you will probably be
impressed with the vastness of
our country, the immensity of
our population and the complexity
of our problems Conditions may
appear different from those pre-
vailing elsewhere. But while
others living close to us may miss
the forest for the trees, gentle-
men, you who have come from
distant lands and are able too
look at our country from a de-
tached point of view are sure to
see it in its proper light. China
is in a period of transition. The
process of rebuilding an old
nation into a new one is in full
swing. More recently, however,
conditions have been greatly
aggravated by military opera-
tion from without, and by the
danger of its continuance or ex-
tension. Without attempting to
give you a picture of the con-
sequence and effect it has pro-
duced upon our national life,
suffice it to say that progress has
been arrested in several phases of
our work of reconstruction and
the conduct of government has
been seriously hampered.
"In the course of your inquiry
you will probably note that there
exists in China to-day a great
deal of animated feeling on the
subject of Sino-Japanese relations.
Upon a more profound study, it
is certain to be found that this
sentiment in China is a direct
and spontaneous reaction against
the use of force as an instrument
of rational policy directed at
China. It is seen expressed in
writing or reflected in speeches
or manifested widely in the dis-
criminating purchase of foreign
goods. But in whatever form it is
the effect of events that have trans-
pired since September 18, its cause
lies outside China and beyond her
control.
"This mission entrusted to this
important Commission, therefore, is
not only a matter of vital concern
to China, but is one in which the
whole world is and must feel deep-
ly interested. Forward-looking
thinkers and statesmen have labor-
ed conscientiously and diligently to
lead the world on to a new path
through the Covenant and the
Peace Pact. Their efficiency as in-
struments of peace and their re-
cognition as sound principles for
international relations are being
put to a severe test, the outcome
of which will cause the world to re-
flect on their practicability, and
determine the trend of its future
development.
"I am confident, however, that
with the unremitting interest and
ceaseless energy of the League de-
voted to the Far Eastern situation
at present, with the hearty co-
operation of the United States
in the preservation of peace and
joint search for a permanent solu-
tion, and with the Commission of
Inquiry working here on the spot, a
way will be found whereby the ter-
ritorial and political integrity of
China will be respected and the
sanctity of the instruments of
peace re-established."
In reply, Lord Lytton on behalf
of the Commission, remarked that
he was very gratified to see that
Dr. Koo had been appointed Asses-
sor to the Commission.

Future Arrangement
It has been decided that, on
principle, all of the official
luncheons, which previously ap-
peared on the programme of the
League Commission, be cancelled.
On the other hand, the number of
business receptions will be increas-
ed—that is to say, more time will
be devoted by the delegates to con-
ferences with various associations.
Owing to circumstances, the
League Commission's programme
cannot be fixed for many days
ahead. Many prominent person-
ages wish to be received and fur-
ther audiences will be arranged at
short notice.
To-night, the League delegates
propose to attend a dinner tender-
ed by the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce of Greater Shanghai.
The day will be spent in making
private calls.
On Saturday night Mr. T. V.
Soong will give a dinner party at
which the Commission will be
present.
It is understood that the Japan-
ese Minister, Mr. M. Shigemitsu,
has invited the Commission to din-
ner or luncheon, but as yet no date
has been fixed. The Japanese
residents wished to arrange a
luncheon for the delegates, but it
has been decided to change the
party to a meeting.
It is expected that the Commis-
sion may remain in Shanghai for
another week or so, although no
definite date of departure has yet
been arranged.

Dr. Koo Visits Lord Lytton
Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo, the
Chinese Assessor, visited Lord
Lytton, chairman of the Commis-
sion of Inquiry, at the Cathay
Hotel yesterday. A long conversa-
tion followed, during which a
cordial exchange of views took
place.

属于中国报业公会的中文报刊有《申报》、《新闻报》、《字林西报》（Eastern Times）、《时事新报》（China Times）和《大陆报》（China Press）。

晚宴
昨晚，顾维钧博士在西摩路 129 号设宴招待国际联盟调查团成员。顾博士在欢迎辞中表示：——
“李顿勋爵及调查团各位尊敬的委员，诸位先生：——作为中国籍顾问，我十分荣幸地向各位致以最热烈的欢迎，欢迎大家来到中国。尽管在座诸位中或许有人是首次造访远东，然而，鉴于各位分别在政治家、军人或外交官领域所取得的杰出成就，我们感觉早已与各位相识。国联真诚地感到欣慰，因为能由如此一群杰出的领袖承担此次调查中日冲突的使命，该冲突最近已引起全世界的关注。欢迎各位来到中国，因为你们是和平与正义的使者。在目前中国的形势下，我们能提供的款待必然是简朴的，但它却是热情而真诚的。
“我们的欢迎之所以热情而真诚，是因为你们来自国际联盟。国联赖以建立的和平原则，正是我们历史和文学中最珍视的原则。数个世纪以来，中国圣贤教导我们‘笔胜于剑’。孔子曰：‘四海之内皆兄弟’。可以说，国联的精神即是中国文明的精神。正因如此，中国是最早批准成立国联的国家之一；而作为中方代表，我有幸先在威尔逊总统的卓越主持下，参与起草盟约委员会的工作，随后在国联成立的最初几年里，列席其理事会和大会。”
“我们问题的复杂性”
顾博士补充道：“自从你们抵达中国这片土地以来，诸位先生可能已经注意到，周围处处充满生机与活力。随着你们行程的深入和见闻的增加，你们可能会对我们幅员之辽阔、人口之众多以及问题之复杂留下深刻印象。这里的状况可能与其他地方 prevailing 的情况有所不同。但是，虽然生活在我们要近的人可能会因只见树木而不见森林，但诸位先生，你们来自远方，能够以超然的视角审视我们的国家，必定能看清其本来面目。中国正处于过渡时期。将一个古老的国家重建为一个新国家的过程正在全面展开。然而，最近局势因外部的军事行动及其持续或扩大的危险而大大恶化。我不打算向你们描绘这些行动对我国国民生活所产生的后果和影响， suffice it to say（ suffice it to say 意为‘ suffice it to say ’，此处依语境译为‘ suffice it to say ’），我国重建工作的几个阶段进展受阻，政府施政受到严重阻碍。
“在调查过程中，你们可能会注意到，当今中国在中日关系问题上存在大量激昂的情绪。经过更深入的研究，可以肯定地发现，中国的这种情绪是对将武力作为对华理性政策工具的直接且自发的反应。这种情绪表现为文字书写、反映在演讲中，或广泛体现于对外国商品的抵制性购买行为上。但无论以何种形式表现，这都是 9 月 18 日以来发生的事件的结果，其原因在中国之外，非中国所能控制。
“因此，委托给这个重要调查团的使命，不仅对中国至关重要，也是全世界深切关注且必须关注的事项。富有远见的思想家和政治家们通过《国联盟约》和《和平公约》，勤勉不懈地努力引导世界走向一条新的道路。它们作为和平工具的有效性，以及作为国际关系健全原则的认可度，正受到严峻考验，其结果将促使世人反思其可行性，并决定世界未来的发展趋势。
“然而，我深信，凭借国联对当前远东局势的持续关注和不懈努力，凭借美国在维护和平及共同寻求永久解决方案方面的衷心合作，再加上调查团在此实地工作，必将找到一条尊重中国领土和政治完整、恢复和平文书神圣性的途径。”
李顿勋爵代表调查团致答辞，表示他对顾博士被任命为调查团顾问感到非常满意。

后续安排
已原则上决定，取消此前列入国联调查团日程的所有官方午宴。另一方面，将增加商务招待会的次数——也就是说，代表们将投入更多时间与各协会进行会谈。由于情况使然，国联调查团的日程无法提前多日确定。许多知名人士希望获得接见，进一步的谒见将在短时间内安排。
今晚，国联代表拟出席上海总商会举办的晚宴。白天将用于私人拜访。
周六晚，宋子文先生将举行晚宴，调查团将出席。
据悉，日本公使重光葵先生已邀请调查团参加晚宴或午宴，但尚未确定日期。日本侨民原希望为代表们安排一次午宴，但已决定将该活动改为会议。
预计调查团可能在上海再停留一周左右，尽管具体的离沪日期尚未安排。

顾博士拜访李顿勋爵
中国籍顾问顾维钧博士昨日在 Cathay Hotel（华懋饭店）拜访了调查团主席李顿勋爵。随后进行了长时间的交谈，期间双方亲切交换了意见。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, March 17, 1932
3380.
1. 3. 32.

Mukden Civic, Educational
Leaders Wire League Group

Hold They Prefer To Share China's Destiny
Than Live Under Japanese Rule In
Message To Lord Lytton

Holding that they have placed their confidence in the League of Nations but adding that they are prepared to fight for the vindication of right over might, a group of Chinese civic heads and leaders in Mukden today forwarded the following message of welcome to the League of Nations Commission of Inquiry, now in Shanghai.

"We, representing the 30,000,000 Chinese people of the Three Eastern Provinces of China, welcome each of you to this much troubled land.

"We welcome you with the warmth of heart which is traditionally Chinese and which, to quote Confucius, always delights in the presence of friends from afar.

Homes Destroyed

"But we are sorry that we shall not be able to welcome you to our humble homes. They have been wantonly destroyed or occupied by our neighbor. See what vandalism that Japanese committed in Shanghai.

"They say they defended themselves but their 'defensive measures' deny us even the birthright of existence.

"See what a fictitious 'paradise' the Japanese have claimed in Manchuria. There, tens of thousands of us were made not only homeless and destitute but were 'protected unto death.'

Not Bandits

"The Japanese call any Chinese a bandit when he shows a bit of national feeling and they continue to manufacture bandits to terrorize the civil population both as an excuse for permanent occupation and as a means to force the masses to welcome their protection.

"We solemnly protest against the brutal Japanese aggression which has outraged and trampled under foot international treaties as well as elementary principles and sentiments of mankind.

'Part Of China'

"The so-called Manchukuo state is purely a puppet of the Japanese Army, a step deliberately designed for the dismemberment of China preparatory to the actual annexation by Japan.

"While recognizing and conscious of our own limitations and shortcomings, we 30,000,000 Chinese reaffirm anew our determination that our homeland, Manchuria, shall be as we are, a part of China and our future indissolubly bound up with her destiny.

"May we assure you, that the labor and counsel of the League of Nations and the United States you represent in behalf of peace, concord and international fair play is deeply appreciated by all the Chinese people.

Remain Confident

"Under the common fatherhood of God, we repose full confidence in your mission which we hope will formulate a solution that is fair and just.

"On the other hand, we are not blind to your difficulties that lie ahead. We will wait and see whether the League, created at painful cost and embodying the hopes of humanity can prove that might is not now the sole test of right.

"Meanwhile we are resolutely prepared to fight for the vindication of right over might.

Many Signers

"Signed: Enchi Chin, President of the Federation of Chambers of Commerce of the Three Eastern Provinces. Ku Ang-chi, president of the labor unions of Mukden. Tsen Tuc-chi, president of the educational Association of Liaoning Province. Chi Feng, President of the Federation of Farmers Associations, Liaoning Province. Mu Ting, chairman of the Mukden's Bankers Association. Chuan Ta-meng, Acting President of the Lawyers Association of Mukden.

"Tu Shih-chao, President of the Press Association of the Three Eastern Provinces. En Cheng-ning, acting President of the Northeastern University. Hsien Li, President of Kirin University. Hua Yi-wang, President of the Federation of Youths of the Three Eastern Provinces. Mrs. Fenghsien Liao-wang, Chairman of the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom, Mukden Branch. Tso Yan-wang, secretary of the League of Nations Society, Mukden Branch, Sherman Soo, Secretary of the Foreign Relations Association of the Three Eastern Provinces. Paul Yen, Secretary of the Christian Association of the Three Eastern Province. Princess Taerhan, President of the Mongolian Culture Association.

"C. F. Wang, Secretary of the Institute of Pacific Relations, Mukden Branch. Mai Fo-kuang, Chairman of the Teachers Association of Mukden. Mao Yun-gen, President of the Northeastern Medical Science Society. Hsiao Chien-chin, Secretary of the Chinese Economic Society, Northeastern Branch. Sun Kao-feng, Director of the China Science Society, Mukden Branch. Chang Tao-fu, Secretary of the Chinese Engineering Association, Northeastern Branch. Ming Kao-chao, Secretary of the Northeastern Political Science Society. Chi Yi-hsueh, President of the Northeastern Mining Association. Harriet Chou, Secretary of the Northeastern Returned Students Association."

P.S. Referred to in to-day's Chinese press translations.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1932 年 3 月 17 日，星期四
3380.
1. 3. 32.

沈阳市民界、教育界领袖致电国联代表团

称宁愿与中国共命运，也不愿在日本统治下生活
致李顿勋爵的电文

沈阳的一批中国市民领袖和负责人今日向目前在上海的国际联盟调查团发出了以下欢迎电文，表示他们对国际联盟充满信心，并补充说他们准备为捍卫正义战胜强权而战。

“我们代表中国东北三省三千万中国人民，欢迎各位来到这片多难之地。

“我们以中国人传统的热情欢迎你们，正如孔子所言，‘有朋自远方来，不亦乐乎’。

家园被毁

“但我们很遗憾，我们无法在寒舍欢迎你们。我们的家园已被邻居肆意摧毁或占领。看看日本人在上海犯下的野蛮行径吧。

“他们声称是自卫，但他们的‘防御措施’甚至剥夺了我们生存的天赋权利。

“看看日本人在满洲宣称的那个虚构的‘天堂’吧。在那里，我们成千上万的人不仅无家可归、陷入贫困，而且被‘保护至死’。

并非匪徒

“日本人将任何表现出一点民族感情的中国人都称为匪徒，并继续制造匪徒以恐吓平民，这既作为永久占领的借口，也作为迫使民众欢迎其保护的手段。

“我们严正抗议日本残暴的侵略行径，这种行为践踏了国际条约以及人类的基本准则和情感。

‘中国的一部分’

“所谓的‘满洲国’纯粹是日本军队的傀儡，是日本为实际吞并中国而精心设计的肢解中国的一个步骤。

“虽然我们认识到并意识到自身的局限性和不足，但我们这三千万中国人再次重申我们的决心：我们的家乡满洲和我们一样，是中国的一部分，我们的未来与中国的命运紧密相连，不可分割。

“请允许我们向你们保证，中国人民深深感激你们所代表的国际联盟和美国为和平、和谐及国际公平竞赛所付出的辛劳和提供的建议。

保持信心

“在上帝的共同父权下，我们对你们的使命充满信心，希望这一使命能制定出一个公平合理的解决方案。

“另一方面，我们也并非看不到你们前方存在的困难。我们将拭目以待，看这个以痛苦代价建立、承载着人类希望的国际联盟，能否证明强权并非如今检验正义的唯一标准。

“同时，我们坚决准备为捍卫正义战胜强权而战。

众多签署人

“签署人：东北三省商会联合会主席陈楚材（Enchi Chin，音译）。沈阳工会主席库安志（Ku Ang-chi，音译）。辽宁省教育协会会长曾叔迟（Tsen Tuc-chi，音译）。辽宁省农会联合会主席季丰（Chi Feng，音译）。沈阳银行公会主席穆廷（Mu Ting，音译）。沈阳律师公会代理会长全达梦（Chuan Ta-meng，音译）。

“东北三省报业公会主席杜世超（Tu Shih-chao，音译）。东北大学代理校长恩成宁（En Cheng-ning，音译）。吉林大学校长鲜丽（Hsien Li，音译）。东北三省青年联合会会长华义旺（Hua Yi-wang，音译）。妇女国际和平与自由联盟沈阳分会主席廖王冯贤夫人（Mrs. Fenghsien Liao-wang，音译）。国联同志社沈阳分会秘书左延旺（Tso Yan-wang，音译）。东北三省外交协会秘书 Sherman Soo（苏谢尔曼，音译）。东北三省基督教协会秘书 Paul Yen（颜保罗，音译）。蒙古文化协会主席达尔罕公主（Princess Taerhan，音译）。

“太平洋关系学会沈阳分会秘书 C. F. Wang（王CF，音译）。沈阳教师协会主席麦福光（Mai Fo-kuang，音译）。东北医学科学会会长毛云根（Mao Yun-gen，音译）。中国经济学会东北分会秘书萧建金（Hsiao Chien-chin，音译）。中国科学社沈阳分社社长孙高峰（Sun Kao-feng，音译）。中国工程师学会东北分会秘书张道甫（Chang Tao-fu，音译）。东北政治学会秘书明高超（Ming Kao-chao，音译）。东北矿业协会会长冀一学（Chi Yi-hsueh，音译）。东北留学生协会秘书 Harriet Chou（周哈丽特，音译）。”

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, MARCH 17, 1932 3390

States Members' Duties
Defined By Chairman Of
League Delegation Here

Lord Lytton Pronounces Policy Of The League Of
Nations In Diplomatic Speech At University
Association Luncheon Party

"PEACE MUST BE IN THEIR HEARTS; NOT
ONLY IN MOUTHS," SAYS LEADER

In a speech that was eloquent of diplomacy and tact. Lord Lytton, leader of the delegation of the League of Nations spoke at the luncheon tendered by the local Universities' Association yesterday. Lord Lytton enumerated some of the conditions which the League of Nations expected its States' Members to observe and honour. "The League expects all of its Members States to feel that it is not in the power of any other State to injure them. But at the same time it requires its members to refrain from all forms of injury to others," he added.

That the League of Nations expects the observance of all laws was stated by the leader of the Geneva delegation, when he stated that in return for protection from aggression, and the maintenance of justice, the League expects that its members shall have "peace in their hearts and not only in their mouths."

Lord Lytton, who responded to the welcome of the Universities' Association, stated:
"I rise to respond on behalf of the members of the Commission of Inquiry, whom you have so kindly invited to meet you here to-day. Will you allow me to speak to you quite informally as a University man to University-men? You have spoken very feelingly of the horror which, in common with many other innocent people, two of your universities have recently experienced, and yet you were able to speak of 'a light above the horizon.'"

"There is a proverb in my country: 'The darkest hour is that which immediately precedes the dawn.' May I be permitted to express the hope that in years to come you will recognize that the present darkness to which you have referred, was of that kind. It is of the dawn rather than the darkness that I want now to speak to you.

Conditions Required
"That light which you already see above the horizon comes, if I understand aright, from the direction of Geneva, and I would therefore like to suggest to you the way in which the League of Nations might help you, and at the same time remind you of the conditions which the League would require in return.
"It is, I think, the purpose of the League to remove fear from the mentality of its States' members by guaranteeing to them protection from aggression and the maintenance of justice. But in return the League expects that its members shall have peace in their hearts and not only in their mouths. It is not possible for any nation to cultivate hatred and hostility toward other countries and then to expect the League to step in and save them from the consequences of that attitude.

"Injury To Others"
"The League expects all its members states to feel that it is not in the power of any other State to injure them. But at the same time it requires its members to refrain from all forms of injury to others. Whatever any State has a right to ask, the League will secure for it, provided it is not obtained at the expense of another. What a State has no right to ask from another, the League will prevent it from taking by force.
"All this may sound to you very philosophical and theoretical. But those are the principles on which the League machinery works. It is for men like you in all countries to make them known to the people. The teachers to-day are the soldiers of to-morrow, and it is to such soldiers that I now raise my glass and drink your health."

Dr. Wang's Speech
At the luncheon Dr. Wang King-yu, president of the National Labour University, and formerly the Chinese delegate to the Council of the League of Nations, welcomed the League delegation. Mr. Wang said:
"In the name of the Association of Universities and Colleges of Shanghai, we have the honour to extend to you our warm welcome. We are aware that during the past weeks and months, the people of the world, imbued with good-will, have heard of the signal of distress from a martyred nation. The efforts they have made to stop bloodshed have fully convinced us of the real existence of a law of nations, and of an institution guarding international peace. However the foreign invasion still submerges us, the numerous enemy aeroplanes are still doing damage without cessation, even on the eve of your arrival, upon our coastal and interior towns, in which thousands of non-combatant women and children, have perished. The systematic destruction of our intellectual centers, the ruin of which you will certainly visit, is yet unabated. In spite of all this, and in spite of the atrocities committed, the friends of Geneva, amongst whom there are many in the Chinese intellectual circles, have not lost their faith, and have longed for an unbiased verdict from the League of Nations.

Question Of Teaching
"During such a difficult time, when human suffering wrought by the last European War, and the deadly fight between various social principles, are still at their height, we, representing the intellectual China of to-day, often ask ourselves what shall we teach our anxious and ardent young generation representing China of to-morrow. We have assumed the grave responsibility of guiding towards the road of right, of wisdom and of international co-operation. In fact, what shall we teach them: shall we teach them to believe in the worship of violence and brutal force, or shall we prove to them that there is an international justice?
"Is there a universal conscience awakening, and revolting against the crimes of inhumanity, and is there a League of Nations guaranteeing the treaties outlawing war?
"We believe that your presence in China and your future impartial enquiries will greatly facilitate the answering of the above questions. The time has now arrived for all to translate the idea of justice and fair-play into realistic and visible acts. With strong hope in our heart we raise our cups to wish you a pleasant sojourn in China, and the success of your noble mission of peace."

Yesterday's Programme
Yesterday, in addition to being entertained at a luncheon party by the local Universities' Association, the League Commission was present at a tea party given jointly by Madame T. V. Soong and Madame Kung Hsiang-hsi, and at a dinner party tendered jointly by the British, American and French Ministers to China, together with the Italian Charge d'Affaires.
The tea party given jointly by Madame Soong and Madame Kung Hsiang-hsi was quite an informal affair. The hostesses arranged an entertaining party and the League Commission and other guests thoroughly enjoyed the function which was held at 383 Rue de Sioyes.

Officials Pay Call
Yesterday the chairmen of the Shanghai Municipal Council, Brig.-Gen. McNaughten, the Director-General, Mr. Stirling Fessenden, and Mr. A. D. Bell, a member of the Council, made official calls on Lord Lytton. This formal call was made at the Cathay Hotel, where Lord Lytton and other members of the League Commission, are staying.

Schedule Altered
To allow the members of the League Commission more respite and thus permit them more time to themselves while in Shanghai, a number of engagements previously appearing on the official programme, have been deleted.
The arrangements for to-day—a lunch with Chinese newspapermen and a dinner tendered by Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo—will stand, and no alterations have been made.
To-morrow, however, the lunch with the Economic Society has been cancelled. The League delegation will be entertained in the evening at a dinner party by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce.
On Saturday, the dinner party arranged by Mr. T. V. Soong, will be held as scheduled. The luncheon which the League Commission was to attend has been deleted from the programme.
Prominent ... give a dinner ... luncheon ...

《字林西报》，1932年3月17日，星期四 3390

国联代表团团长在此界定
成员国义务

李顿勋爵在大学协会午餐会上发表外交演说
阐述国际联盟政策

“和平须存于心，不仅止于口”，领袖言道

在昨日由本地大学协会举办的午餐会上，国际联盟代表团团长李顿勋爵（Lord Lytton）发表了一篇充满外交辞令与机智的演讲。李顿勋爵列举了国际联盟期望其成员国遵守并信守的一些条件。“国联期望所有成员国都感到，任何其他国家都无力伤害它们。但与此同时，国联要求其成员克制对他人的一切形式的伤害，”他补充道。

日内瓦代表团团长指出，国联期望所有法律得到遵守。他表示，作为免受侵略和维护正义的回报，国联期望其成员“心中拥有和平，而不仅仅是嘴上说说”。

李顿勋爵在回应大学协会的欢迎辞时 stated：
“我起身代表调查委员会成员作答谢，承蒙各位盛情邀请他们今日在此与各位会面。请允许我以一名大学人的身份，非正式地与各位大学同仁交谈。你们非常动情地谈到了两所大学近期与许多其他无辜民众共同经历的恐怖遭遇，然而你们仍能提及‘地平线上的一缕光明’。”

“我国有一句谚语：‘黎明前是最黑暗的时刻。’请允许我表达这样的希望：在未来的岁月里，你们会认识到，你们所提及的当前黑暗正是那种性质。我现在想与各位谈论的是黎明，而非黑暗。

所需条件
“如果我的理解正确，你们已在地平线上看到的那缕光明来自日内瓦方向，因此我想向各位建议国际联盟可能帮助你们的方式，同时提醒各位国联为此所要求的条件。
“我认为，国联的宗旨是通过保证成员国免受侵略和维护正义，从而消除其成员国心理上的恐惧。但作为回报，国联期望其成员心中拥有和平，而不仅仅是嘴上说说。任何国家都不可能在培育对他国的仇恨和敌意之后，又指望国联介入并将其从这种态度的后果中拯救出来。

‘对他人的伤害’
“国联期望所有成员国都感到，任何其他国家都无力伤害它们。但与此同时，国联要求其成员克制对他人的一切形式的伤害。无论任何国家有权要求什么，只要不以牺牲他国为代价，国联都将为其确保。对于一国无权向他国索取的东西，国联将阻止其以武力夺取。
“这一切在各位听来可能非常哲学化和理论化。但这些正是国联机制运作的原则。让各国人民了解这些原则，是像各位这样的人的责任。今天的教师就是明天的战士，我现在举杯向这样的战士们致敬，祝各位健康。”

王博士的演讲

在午餐会上，国立劳动大学校长、前国际联盟理事会中国代表王京钰（Wang King-yu，音译）博士欢迎了国联代表团。王先生说：
“谨代表上海各大学及学院协会，我们荣幸地向各位表示热烈欢迎。我们深知，在过去几周和几个月里，怀着善意的世界人民听到了一个受难民族发出的求救信号。他们为制止流血所作努力，使我们充分确信国际法的真实存在，以及有一个维护国际和平的机构。然而，外敌入侵仍使我们深陷苦难，众多敌机仍在不断肆虐，甚至在各位抵达前夕，仍对我们的沿海和内陆城镇进行轰炸，导致成千上万非战斗人员的妇女和儿童丧生。对我们智力中心的系统性破坏——各位肯定会去参观那些废墟——仍未停止。尽管如此，尽管暴行累累，日内瓦的朋友们——其中在中国知识界不乏其人——并未失去信心，并渴望得到国际联盟公正的裁决。

教育问题
“在这个艰难时期，上一次欧洲战争造成的人类苦难以及各种社会原则之间的殊死斗争仍处于高潮，我们代表当今中国的知识界，常常自问：我们应该教导代表明日中国的焦虑而热情的年轻一代什么？我们承担了引导他们走向正道、智慧和国际合作的重大责任。事实上，我们应该教给他们什么：是教他们崇拜暴力和野蛮力量，还是向他们证明存在国际正义？
“普遍的良知是否正在觉醒，反抗不人道的罪行？是否存在一个保障废除战争条约的国际联盟？
“我们相信，各位莅临中国以及未来公正的调查，将极大地促进上述问题的解答。现在是将正义和公平竞赛的理念转化为现实且可见行动的时候了。我们怀着强烈的希望举杯，祝愿各位在中国逗留愉快，并祝各位崇高的和平使命取得成功。”

昨日活动安排

昨日，除参加本地大学协会举办的午餐会外，国联调查委员会还出席了由宋子文夫人和孔祥熙夫人联合举办的茶会，以及由英国、美国和法国驻华公使连同意大利代办联合举办的晚宴。
由宋夫人和孔夫人联合举办的茶会气氛相当轻松。东道主安排了一场令人愉快的聚会，国联调查委员会及其他宾客在位于思义路383号（Rue de Sioyes）举行的活动中尽享乐趣。

官员拜访

昨日，上海公共租界工部局总董麦克诺滕准将（Brig.-Gen. McNaughten）、总办费森登先生（Mr. Stirling Fessenden）以及董事贝尔先生（Mr. A. D. Bell）对李顿勋爵进行了正式拜访。这次正式拜访是在李顿勋爵及国联调查委员会其他成员下榻的华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel）进行的。

日程变更

为了让国联调查委员会成员在上海期间有更多的休息时间和个人支配时间，原官方日程中的一些活动已被取消。
今日的安排——与中国报界人士共进午餐，以及顾维钧博士（Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo）举办的晚宴——照常进行，未作更改。
然而，明日与经济学会的午餐会已取消。晚上，国联代表团将出席由中国商会举办的晚宴。
周六，由宋子文先生（Mr. T. V. Soong）安排的晚宴将按计划举行。原计划由国联调查委员会参加的午餐会从日程中删除。
知名人士……举办晚宴……午餐……

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 16, 1932 389
LEAGUE COMMISSION FETED
BY OFFICIALS
Many Receptions Given in Honour of
International Inquiry Body
A DAY OF SPEECHES
Lord Lytton Defines Attitude and Powers
of Geneva Council
THE first day in Shanghai of the League of Nations Commission of Inquiry into the Far Eastern crisis proved to be very busy, the Commission wasting no time in getting into touch with Chinese leaders.
First paying official calls on Mr. T. V. Soong, Minister of Finance, Mr. Quo Tai-chi, Political Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs and General Wu Te-chen, Mayor of Greater Shanghai, the Commission were entertained to tiffin by Mr. Quo. In the evening they were guests at a reception given by Dr. Wellington Koo and concluded the day by being entertained to dinner by General Wu Te-chen, Mayor of Greater Shanghai.
Mr. Quo Tai-chi in a speech yesterday referred to the co-operation which the League had given China in the past few years, and hoped that by such fruitful co-operation peace might come to China, while Lord Lytton, Chairman of the Commission, referred to the difficulties in front of the Commission but voiced his belief that difficulties are made to overcome.
FULL PROGRAMME TO-DAY
To-day it is expected that the Commission will again have a full programme, although last night it had not been definitely decided upon. Private talks and interviews will probably form a large part of the Commission's work, rather than any public meeting.
The time that the Commission will stay in Shanghai has not been definitely decided, as there is a great deal for the Commission to see and hear in the Shanghai Area.
The members of the Commission are the Earl of Lytton, P.C., G.C.S.I., G.C.I.E., Great Britain, General Henri Claudel of France, Count Luigi Aldrovandi Marescotti of Italy, Dr. Albert H. H. Schnee of Germany and Major-General Frank Ross McCoy of the United States. With them are several assistants, Mr. Haas being the Secretary-General to the Commission, and Dr. A. Pelt, Assistant Secretary-General.
Yesterday morning officials calls were paid by members of the Commission on Mr. T. V. Soong, Minister of Finance, Mr. Quo Tai-chi, and General Wu Te-chen, after which they were entertained to tiffin by Mr. Quo.
At the tiffin, Mr. Quo Tai-chi spoke as follows:—
Lord Lytton and Honourable members of the League Commission,—Owing to the abnormal and unprecedented circumstances which have prevailed in this Shanghai area in recent weeks, it has been necessary for me to spend most of my time here instead of at Nanking, and it is on this account that the duty and privilege devolve upon me today to extend, on behalf of the National Government, the first official hospitality to you as members of the Commission of Inquiry which has been created by the League of Nations to visit China.
To assist me in welcoming you today, I have asked the leading members of the Chinese civic and business community in this metropolis of international commerce to
parts of the world since more than ten years ago it was first formed. It has had many difficulties to contend with, and has been called upon to solve not a few crises, and I think I am justified in saying that it has never failed yet. It is because of that experience that we feel justified in our faith that we shall not fail on this occasion.—(Applause).
Members of the Commission then drank to the health of their hosts.
Big Reception
Members of the League Commission were guests at a reception given by Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo at 1550 Bubbling Well Road yesterday evening. A large number of people attended representing every phase of official and civilian life in Shanghai.
Mayor Entertains
At a dinner given by him at the Cathay Hotel last night to members of the Commission, General Wu Te-chen, Mayor of Greater Shanghai, spoke as follows:—
Gentlemen, It gives me, as Mayor of Greater Shanghai, great honour and pleasure to extend our sincere welcome to the distinguished mem-
ly arrested by the astounding chain of events since the coup in our Three Eastern Provinces known as manchuria last September.
Our earnest hope and desire are that, as the outcome of your self-denying labours, the peace of the Orient may be restored and a durable understanding reached, under the aegis of the League and the Briand-Kellogg Pact, whereby the Chinese Republic—comprising some 400 millions homogeneous people—may live in honorable and friendly relations with her neighbours, and be free to develop her own national life so as to contribute whatever she may be capable of in the pursuits of peace towards the progress and advancement of mankind.
Lord Lytton Replies
Lord Lytton, in reply stated:—Your Excellency. On behalf of the members of the Commission of Inquiry I offer you, in their name, our most grateful thanks for your hospitality. This is for us a particularly interesting occasion, for it is, if I may use the phrase, our first appearance on the stage in China. We had the pleasure and advantage of being entertained by your Consul-General in Tokyo, but that was, if I may continue the metaphor, back in the wings. We are now fully in the limelight, as we have recently experienced and feel that our work has begun in earnest. With the addition of Dr. Wellington Koo to our numbers we feel that the Commission is now complete, and on this, our first appearance in China, I desire to thank you, Sir, for the spirit in which you have welcomed us.
In the remarks you have just addressed to us you have expressed the interest of China in the work of the League, the loyalty with which the principles of the League are supported in China, and you have told us also that in the past you have had no small faith by experience. 《字林西报》，1932年3月16日，星期三 389
官员宴请国联调查团
为国际调查机构举行多次招待会
演讲之日
李顿勋爵阐述日内瓦理事会之立场与权限

国际联盟远东危机调查委员会在上海的第一天证明是非常忙碌的，该委员会抓紧时间与中国领导人取得联系。

调查团首先正式拜访了财政部长宋子文先生、外交部政务次长郭泰祺先生以及大上海市长吴铁城将军，随后郭泰祺先生设午宴款待调查团。晚间，他们作为顾维钧博士举行的招待会的宾客出席，并由大上海市长吴铁城将军设晚宴款待，以此结束了一天的行程。

郭泰祺先生在昨日的演讲中提到了国联在过去几年给予中国的合作，并希望透过这种富有成效的合作，和平能降临中国；而调查团主席李顿勋爵则提到了调查团面临的困难，但表示相信困难正是为了被克服而存在的。

今日日程满满

预计今天调查团的日程将再次排满，尽管昨晚尚未最终确定。私下谈话和访谈可能会构成调查团工作的大部分，而非任何公开会议。

调查团在上海停留的时间尚未最终确定，因为调查团在上海地区有大量需要视察和听取的事项。

调查团成员包括：英国代表李顿伯爵（P.C., G.C.S.I., G.C.I.E.）、法国代表亨利·克劳德尔将军（General Henri Claudel）、意大利代表路易吉·阿尔德罗万迪·马雷斯科蒂伯爵（Count Luigi Aldrovandi Marescotti）、德国代表阿尔伯特·H·H·施内博士（Dr. Albert H. H. Schnee）以及美国代表弗兰克·罗斯·麦考伊少将（Major-General Frank Ross McCoy）。随行的还有数名助理，其中哈斯先生（Mr. Haas）担任调查团秘书长，A·佩尔特博士（Dr. A. Pelt）担任副秘书长。

昨天上午，调查团成员正式拜访了财政部长宋子文先生、郭泰祺先生以及吴铁城将军，随后郭泰祺先生设午宴款待他们。

在午宴上，郭泰祺先生致辞如下：——

李顿勋爵及国联调查团的各位尊贵成员，——由于近几周来上海地区局势异常且史无前例，我不得不将大部分时间花在这里，而非南京，正因如此，今天我才有责任和荣幸代表国民政府，向作为国联派往中国的调查委员会成员的诸位，致以首次官方款待。

为了协助我今天欢迎诸位，我邀请了这座国际商业大都市的中国市民界和商界的主要成员……

自十多年前国联最初成立以来……世界各地。它曾面临许多困难，并被要求解决不少危机，我认为我有理由说，它迄今从未失败过。正是基于这一经验，我们有理由相信此次也不会失败。（掌声）

随后，调查团成员举杯祝主人健康。

盛大招待会

昨晚，国联调查团成员作为顾维钧（V. K. Wellington Koo）博士在静安寺路1550号举行的招待会的宾客出席。众多代表上海官方和民间生活各个层面的人士参加了此次盛会。

市长设宴款待

昨晚，大上海市长吴铁城将军在 Cathay Hotel（华懋饭店/国泰饭店）为调查团成员举行晚宴，并致辞如下：——

诸位先生，作为大上海市长，我感到极大的荣幸和愉快，向尊贵的成员们表达我们诚挚的欢迎……

自去年九月我们在被称为满洲的东三省发生政变以来，这一连串令人震惊的事件使我们措手不及。

我们恳切的希望和愿望是，作为诸位不辞辛劳工作的成果，东方的和平得以恢复，并在国联和《白里安-凯洛格公约》的庇护下达成持久的谅解，从而使拥有约四亿同质人口的中华民国能够与邻国保持体面友好的关系，并自由发展其民族生活，以便在追求和平的过程中，为人类的进步和发展贡献其力所能及的力量。

李顿勋爵答辞

李顿勋爵在答辞中表示：——阁下。我代表调查委员会的成员，以他们的名义向您致以最感激的谢意，感谢您的盛情款待。对我们来说，这是一个特别有趣的场合，因为如果允许我使用这个比喻的话，这是我们在“中国舞台”上的首次亮相。我们曾在东京有幸得到贵国总领事的款待，但如果继续这个比喻，那是在“幕后”。现在我们完全处于“聚光灯”下，因为我们最近已经体验到并感觉到我们的工作已认真展开。随着顾维钧博士加入我们的行列，我们感到调查团现已阵容完整，在此，我们在华首次亮相之际，我要感谢阁下欢迎我们的精神。

在您刚才对我们的讲话中，您表达了中国对国联工作的兴趣，以及中国支持国联原则的忠诚，您还告诉我们，过去你们通过经验建立了不小的信心。你们意识到，在许多方面，派出的顾问……

From 1928 onwards we have

First, we had the visit of M. Thomas,

Since then there has not been a

has sent us year after year experts

There have been about thirty

我们将把我们权力范围内可提供的信息置于诸位支配之下。

国联的发展

自1927年南京国民政府成立以来，我们的目光便转向日内瓦，关注国联这一组织的发展，将其视为战后促进日益相互依赖和交织的世界的道德与物质福利的重要工具。

从1928年起，我们在国家重建计划中稳步寻求国联的建议与合作。首先，国际劳工局局长托马斯先生（M. Thomas）来访。几个月后，国联副秘书长阿韦诺尔先生（M. Avenol）接踵而至。

此后，每一年国联都与我们真诚合作。它年复一年地向我们派遣公共卫生、教育、劳工、工程和金融方面的专家，在他们的协助下，各种项目得以实施或启动。

此类专家约有三十位，我可以提及亚瑟·索尔特爵士（Sir Arthur Salter）、拉赫曼博士（Dr. Rachjman）（音译）、罗伯特·哈斯先生（M. Robert Haas）、亨利·博内特先生（M. Henri Bonnett）、C·博尔契奇博士（Dr. C. Borcic）以及约翰·霍普·辛普森爵士（Sir John Hope Simpson）。

去年春天，政府决定成立最高经济委员会，设想与国联进行明确合作，并派遣专家协助执行一项全面且可行的国家工作方案，以加速本国的现代化进程。随后，去年夏天特大洪灾席卷了我们大片最美的地区，国联专家就在身边协助我们应对灾难。

获得合作

我们将寻求并获得国联尽可能密切的合作，几乎作为一项基本政策，以应对我们巨大的国家复兴任务。

正如在场的市民和商界领袖所证实的那样，政府的政策得到了人民最衷心的支持。我们期待并将继续期待国联与本国在和平艺术领域的富有成效的合作——尽管暂时……

国联成员，
此外，我们拥有向中国民众介绍国联经验的经历，这也进一步鼓舞了我们。我们作为使者——作为国联的代表而来，将国联的所有资源置于诸位支配之下，在这一特定危机中，只要诸位告知我们如何提供服务，我们就愿意提供其帮助和协助。

并非超国家实体

但我必须提醒诸位，国联不是一个超国家实体；它不能将意志强加于不需要其援助的成员国。国联对武力没有有效的应对之策；它是武力的替代方案。因此，如果这两个大国愿意接受这种替代方案，并利用国联可支配的机制，那么我确实相信这能对双方都有帮助和益处。

我们充分意识到肩负在我们调查团身上的重大责任；我们也充分意识到我们面临的任务的巨大困难，但我们相信困难正是为了被克服而存在的，阁下，您的演讲极大地鼓舞了我们，让我们相信只要双方抱有善意，本案中的困难是可以克服的。

也许我们是乐观的，但我们的乐观植根于信念。我们对国联的力量、对国联作为世界和平工具的价值有着深厚的信念；而这种信念，像阁下一样，是基于经验的。我们一直关注国联在所有……

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, MARCH 15, 1932
3449

League Commission May
Aid In Settling Strife
In Shanghai's Locality

LORD LYTTON PROMISES CO-OPERATION IF
HE AND COLLEAGUES ARE GIVEN
INVITATION TO NEGOTIATIONS

ENTHUSIASTIC WELCOME IS GIVEN TO
DISTINGUISHED DIPLOMATIC PARTY

Scores Of Officials Wait In Chill Of Evening
For Liner Bearing International Group
Whose Mission Is To Bring Peace

With clear skies and bright stars an augury of fair weather, the five men who will endeavour to guide the Far East's floundering political ship into a peaceful haven, arrived in Shanghai last night. Lord Lytton and the other four members of the League of Nations Commission of Inquiry, were enthusiastically greeted by a cosmopolitan crowd of officers and international representatives. British, American, French, Italian, German, Japanese and Chinese thronged to welcome the party. They swarmed about them aboard the liner, President Adams, and clung close to them on the launch that carried the delegates ashore. Shortly before 9 o'clock the Commission landed.

All that Lord Lytton, as chairman and spokesman for the Commission, could say last night, was that he and his colleagues would assist, if invited, in solving the present difficulties between China and Japan.

"We will offer our best co-operation if we are invited to assist the negotiations between the nations concerned," he said. But further he would not go. As to the length of time the Commission would remain in Shanghai,

Lord Lytton made it plain that that was a matter which circumstances would decide.

"Until we have talked with persons who know the situation here, it is impossible to tell just how long we shall remain," he said.

The President Adams was late in docking. For more than an hour members of the welcoming committee waited on the wharf and aboard tenders, nipped by the wind, a little impatient and a little nervous. The Chinese were anxious to make a good impression. And there were so many difficulties. The Dollar Line docks, on the Bund side, are bare, uninviting and cold, like any other piers. There was a police guard of honour, made up of about 100 picked men of the Nantao force, accompanied by a police band, and two national standards. The men had been waiting for a long time on the dock and they were cold. The bandsmen's fingers were numb.

A tender, which had gone down river to meet the liner from Japan, was packed with officials, army and navy officers, white people and Chinese. A number came alongside the wharf just below the office of the President Adams. There was a little confusion then. Chinese police and soldiers tried to control the movement of the people.

Slowly, ablaze with light, the big ship steamed in close and nestled to the pier. The Chinese band struck up some lively air and a steam "donkey" pushed the elevated gangway into place. Immediately there was a rush to the steps. A dense throng waited there to climb aboard the liner.

Delegates Surrounded

When the army of officials had finally got aboard, they surrounded Lord Lytton and his party in a small reception hall. Men and women were packed in there. There was bustle and feverish straining to press through to the front of the crowd. Important gentlemen were striving to get close enough to get an introduction. Dignified persons were shouldered and bundled aside. There was bowing and hand-shaking, formalities and banalities. Lord Lytton suddenly moved towards the doorway. It was time for the tenders to leave for the Bund.

With Lord Lytton were the following gentlemen of the commission:—General Henri Claudel, France; Count Luigi Aldrovandi Marescotti, Italy; Dr. Heinrich Schnee, Germany, and General Frank McCoy, United States.

Leading the party which welcomed the distinguished statesmen were Mayor Wu Teh-chen, Mr. Quo Tai-chi, Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs for China, Dr. Wellington Koo, Dr. Hass, of the League of Nations Communications Department; Col. Tchang Veng, representing the Ministry of War; Capt. L. C. Tseng, of the Ministry of Navy, as well as a number of British, French, American, Italian, Japanese and other Chinese officers. Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten, chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, Col. Thomas, officer commanding the S.V.C., and Major Gerrard, commissioner of police, were also present.

Posed On Docks

The commission members posed as they stepped from the gangway, for a battery of cameramen. Chinese guards in the background stood stiffly. The band played. Sentries nearer to the group walked up and down with drawn automatics. It seemed there was a certain air of apprehension. There were foreign plain-clothes officers amongst the crowd.

Newspapermen were interested in the preparations which obviously anticipated some sort of unpleasantness. Inquiry elicited the information that Nantao authorities had, early in the day, given passes to nearly 200 students to go aboard the Dollar Line tender and meet the liner. It was their intention to make some sort of demonstration, police believed. No one knew precisely what had become of the students. They did not get aboard the tender and there were reports that they had hired their own craft.

"But what sort of trouble is expected?" an officer was asked. "I don't know," he answered. "But we can never tell."

At no time was there any hint of animosity in any direction. Only when Lord Lytton had landed and was walking towards the Bund, there was a cry from a crowd of welcomers who, some said, were Communists. But they seemed only friendly. They bore banners which expressed a hope for peace and expressed their goodwill towards the League of Nations representatives.

Lord Lytton and his group went straight to the Cathay Hotel, and were joined at dinner by several distinguished persons who had come to greet them.

Chorus Of Welcome

The Chinese Press burst forth to-day with a chorus of welcome to greet the members of the League Commission of Inquiry. According to a survey by the Kuo Min News Agency, all the principal dailies, "Shun Pao," "Sin Wan Pao," "China Times" and "Eastern Times," besides playing up in prominent type news of the impending arrival of the Commission, devote columns of editorial comment to an exposition of the hopes entertained by the Chinese nation towards the Commission.

"Our hope is extremely simple and prosaic," the "China Times" declares. "It is our firm conviction that the League Covenant and the Anti-War Pact provide the ideal means of preserving world peace, promoting the common weal of humanity and settling of international disputes. What we demand is simply, and nothing more than, the preservation of our State sovereignty, independence, and our territorial and political integrity—a condition of things which underlies and is guaranteed by, the Nine-Power Washington Treaty."

《字林西报》，1932年3月15日，星期二
3449

国联委员会或可协助
解决上海本地冲突

李顿勋爵承诺，若他及其同事获邀参与谈判，将予以合作

外交显要团受到热烈欢迎

众多官员在傍晚的寒意中等待载有国际代表团的邮轮，该团使命在于带来和平

天空晴朗，星光灿烂，预示着好天气。昨晚，五位致力于引导远东这艘在政治风浪中颠簸的航船驶入和平港湾的人士抵达上海。李顿勋爵（Lord Lytton）及国际联盟调查委员会的其他四位成员，受到了由各国官员和国际代表组成的多元化人群的热烈欢迎。英国、美国、法国、意大利、德国、日本和中国人士云集，欢迎该团。他们涌上“亚当斯总统号”（President Adams）邮轮，围聚在他们身边，并在将代表们送上岸的接驳艇上紧紧相随。委员会于九点前不久登陆。

昨晚，作为委员会主席兼发言人，李顿勋爵所能表示的仅是：若获邀请，他和他的同事将协助解决当前中日之间的困难。

他说：“若获邀协助有关国家之间的谈判，我们将提供最好的合作。”但他不愿再多言。至于委员会将在上海停留多久，

李顿勋爵明确表示，这将视情况而定。

他说：“在我们与了解当地局势的人士交谈之前，无法确切告知我们将停留多久。”

“亚当斯总统号”邮轮靠岸较晚。欢迎委员会的成员在码头和接驳艇上等待了一个多小时，寒风刺骨，略显不耐烦和紧张。中方急于留下良好印象。然而困难重重。位于外滩一侧的美商轮船公司（Dollar Line）码头光秃秃的，缺乏吸引力且寒冷，与其他码头无异。现场有一支由南市警察部队精选的约100名警员组成的仪仗队，伴有警乐队和两面国旗。警员们在码头上等候已久，浑身冻僵。乐队成员的手指也已麻木。

一艘此前驶往下游去迎接从日本驶来的邮轮的接驳艇上，挤满了官员、海陆军军官、白人和中国人。数艘接驳艇靠近码头，停泊在“亚当斯总统号”办公室下方的位置。当时出现了一点混乱。中国警察和士兵试图控制人群的行动。

巨大的邮轮灯火通明，缓缓驶近并紧靠码头。中国乐队奏起欢快的曲调，一台蒸汽绞车将高架舷梯推到位。人们立即冲向台阶。密集的人群在那里等待登上邮轮。

代表被包围

当大批官员最终登船后，他们在一个小接待厅里包围了李顿勋爵及其随行人员。男女拥挤其中。现场一片忙乱，人们狂热地努力挤到人群前方。重要绅士们竭力靠近以获得引见。庄重的人士被推搡到一旁。到处是鞠躬、握手、礼节性的寒暄和客套话。李顿勋爵突然向门口走去。接驳艇该出发前往外滩了。

与李顿勋爵同行的委员会成员如下：法国亨利·克劳德尔将军（General Henri Claudel）；意大利路易吉·阿尔德罗万迪·马雷斯科蒂伯爵（Count Luigi Aldrovandi Marescotti）；德国海因里希·施内博士（Dr. Heinrich Schnee）；以及美国弗兰克·麦考伊将军（General Frank McCoy）。

率领欢迎这位杰出政治家代表团的人员包括：市长吴铁城先生、中国外交部次长郭泰祺先生、顾维钧博士、国联通讯部的哈斯博士（Dr. Hass）、代表军政部的张猛上校（Col. Tchang Veng，音译）、海军部的曾乐春上尉（Capt. L. C. Tseng，音译），以及许多英国、法国、美国、意大利、日本和其他中国军官。上海公共租界工部局董事会主席麦克纳格顿准将（Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten）、上海义勇军指挥官托马斯上校（Col. Thomas）和警务处处长杰拉德少校（Major Gerrard）也出席了活动。

在码头留影

委员会成员走下舷梯时，在一群摄影师面前摆姿势拍照。背景中的中国卫兵僵硬地站立着。乐队演奏着。靠近该群体的哨兵手持出鞘的手枪来回巡逻。似乎弥漫着某种忧虑的气氛。人群中混有外国便衣警员。

记者们对显然预见到某种不愉快事件的准备工作很感兴趣。经询问得知，南市当局当天早些时候已向近200名学生发放通行证，允许他们登上美商轮船公司的接驳艇去迎接邮轮。警方认为，他们的意图是进行某种示威。无人确切知道这些学生的下落。他们并未登上接驳艇，有报告称他们租用了自己的船只。

有人问一名警官：“预计会发生什么样的麻烦？”他回答：“我不知道。但我们永远无法预料。”

任何时候都没有任何方向表现出敌意的迹象。只有当李顿勋爵登陆并走向外滩时，一群欢迎者中有人呼喊，据某些人称他们是共产党人。但他们似乎只是出于友好。他们举着表达和平希望并向国联代表表示善意的横幅。

李顿勋爵及其一行人直接前往华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel），几位前来问候他们的显要人士加入共进晚餐。

欢迎之声

中国报纸今天纷纷发表文章，以一片欢迎之声迎接国联调查委员会成员。据国民新闻社（Kuo Min News Agency）调查，所有主要日报，包括《申报》、《新闻报》、《时事新报》和《大晚报》，除了以显著字体突出报道委员会即将抵达的消息外，还刊登长篇社论，阐述中华民族对委员会寄予的希望。

《时事新报》宣称：“我们的希望极其简单且平凡。我们坚信，《国联盟约》和《非战公约》提供了维护世界和平、促进人类共同福祉以及解决国际争端的理想手段。我们所要求的仅仅是，且不过是，维护我们的国家主权、独立以及领土和政治完整——这是《九国华盛顿条约》所奠定基础并予以保障的状态。”

pages.en:
Continuing, the paper says:
"What we venture to expect of
members of the Commission is
simply that they will assess and
judge all the facts of this com-
plicated and extraordinary case,
as well as all arguments pro and
con relating thereto, strictly in
the light of the letter and spirit
of the League Covenant, the
Anti-War Pact and the Nine-
Power Treaty......China has no
desire to prejudice the judgment
of the Commission with any pre-
conceived views. She is ready to
accept and abide by the verdict
of international law and agree-
ments, of international right and
wrong. It is our firm belief that
the distinguished members of the
commission, who are arriving here
to-day will prove themselves the
strongest champions of interna-
tional law and justice, and that
with their unquestioned ability
and impartiality, they will be
able to fully establish the rights
and wrongs of the case."

Covenant Guides

After extending a cordial wel-
come to the Commission, the
"Shun Pao" points out that the
Commission represents, not any
of the parties to the dispute, but
the impartial and disinterested
League of Nations. In the carry-
ing out of its difficult task, the
Commission must of necessity
look to the League Covenant for
guidance.

One of the underlying princi-
ples of the League Covenant, the
paper continues, is the absolute
equality of member-States in the
eyes of the Covenant. This
principle, it recalls, had been un-
equivocally re-affirmed by M.
Briand, the late distinguished
French statesman, during the
Greco-Bulgarian controversy of
1925. The contention made by
Japan that China is not an "or-
ganized state" and is thus not
entitled to equal treatment as a
member of the League is there-
fore entirely untenable.

Continuing, the "Shun Pao" re-
calls with gratification the de-
claration made by the Commis-
sion during its recent sojourn at
Tokyo that it will carry out its
duties strictly in the position of
an unbiased third party. The
paper expresses confidence that
the Commission will adhere
throughout its work to this cor-
rect attitude.

Mutual respect by the members
of the League for each other's
territorial and political integrity,
the paper continues, lies at the
very foundation of the League.
Article X of the Covenant which
guarantees this integrity forms
therefore the most important pro-
vision of the League's Constitu-
tion. The paper then recalls the
appeal made by the Council to
Japan, in which the principles of
Article X were re-affirmed and a
declaration was made that no
violation of this Article would be
recognized as valid.

Have High Hopes

While deploring that the cum-
bersome procedure by which
League action has been hamper-
ed, has resulted in the present
"impasse," the paper expresses
the hope that the Commission
will carry out its task under the
guidance of this fundamental
principle of the Covenant so that
the discrepancy between facts and
law may be rectified.

After pointing out that China
has unreservedly placed her case
in the hands of the League and
that the vindication of the League
Covenant, the Kellogg-Briand
Pact and the Nine-Power Treaty
will rest upon the shoulders of
the Commission, the "Sin Wan
Pao" proceeds to an investigation
of the causes of the present con-
troversy.

In the first place, the paper
points out, Japan will probably cite
as a justification of her actions
the anti-Japanese boycott in
China and the prevalence of so-
called anti-Japanese feeling. Such
a contention will, however, im-
mediately fall to the ground if
one remembers that the boycott
movement was aroused by the
massacre of Chinese in Korea
and later intensified by the
invasion of Manchuria by the
Japanese forces.

Secondly, the "Sin Wan Pao"
continues, Japan will probably
contend that the immediate cause
of the Manchuria situation was
the alleged destruction done to
the South Manchuria Railway
by Chinese troops. Leaving aside
the fact that such an allegation
has never been proved, it is obvi-
ous that even had such an act
of sabotage actually been com-
mitted, it could easily have been
settled through diplomatic negoti-
ation. How could this be a justi-
fication for the large-scale mili-
tary actions indulged in by the
Japanese? In this connection,
the paper points out that the
Japanese invasion is obviously the
result of a premeditated plan as
has been borne out by the sub-
sequent developments and testified
to by disinterested observers,
including the well-known Dr.
Eddy.

More Argument

Thirdly, the paper points out
that Japan is apparently trying
to cover up her acts of military
aggression by setting up the pres-
ent puppet government in Man-
churia. It is, however, a patent
fact which even the Japanese
have hardly tried to conceal that
members of the puppet govern-
ment have been coerced into doing
what they have now done by the
Japanese military and civil au-
thorities. Thus, even if Japan
should withdraw her troops to the
South Manchuria Railway zone,
she cannot evade her responsibil-
ity for violating China's territorial
and political integrity.

In the fourth place, the "Sin
Wan Pao" declares that while the
task of the Commission is per-
haps confined to Manchuria, it
will probably also investigate into
the Shanghai catastrophe now
that it has arrived here. One of
the justifications of her invasion
of Shanghai that Japan will ad-
vance will probably be the alleged
murder of certain Japanese
monks. Now this case was also
susceptible of ordinary diplomatic
settlement, without having re-
course to the use of force. What
is especially preposterous is that
Japan's invasion was launched
after the Mayor of Greater
Shanghai had unconditionally ac-
cepted the Japanese demands—an
acceptance which even the Japan-
ese Consul himself admitted was
"satisfactory for the time being."
The wanton destruction of the
lives of defenceless non-combat-
ants and cultural institutions in
Shanghai which followed the
Japanese invasion constitute not
only a violation of international
peace agreements but the flouting
of civilized methods of warfare
and thus a crime against human-
ity, the paper concludes.—Kuo
Min.

该报接着称：
“我们斗胆期望调查团委员所做的，仅仅是严格依据《国联盟约》、《非战公约》及《九国公约》的字面含义与精神，对这一复杂且非同寻常案件的所有事实，以及与此相关的所有正反论点，进行评估和裁决……中国无意以任何先入为主的观点来影响调查团的判断。她准备接受并遵守国际法与协定、国际是非准则的裁决。我们坚信，今日抵达此地的调查团诸位杰出委员，将证明自己是国际法与正义的最坚定捍卫者，并凭借其无可置疑的能力与公正性，能够充分厘清本案的是非曲直。”

盟约为纲

《申报》在向调查团表示热烈欢迎后指出，调查团代表的并非争端任何一方，而是公正无私的国际联盟。在执行其艰巨任务时，调查团必然要以《国联盟约》为指引。

该报续称，《国联盟约》的基本原则之一，是盟约面前会员国绝对平等。该报回顾称，已故法国著名政治家白里安（M. Briand）先生在1925年希保争议期间曾 unequivocally 重申这一原则。因此，日本声称中国并非“有组织之国家”，因而无权作为国联成员享受平等待遇的说法，完全站不住脚。

《申报》接着欣慰地回顾，调查团近期在东京逗留期间曾声明，将严格以不偏不倚的第三方立场履行职责。该报表示相信，调查团在整个工作过程中将坚持这一正确态度。

该报续称，国联成员相互尊重彼此的领土完整与政治完整，是国联的基石。保障这种完整的《盟约》第十条，因此构成国联宪章中最重要的条款。该报随后回顾了理事会向日本发出的呼吁，其中重申了第十条的原则，并声明任何违反该条的行为均不被视为有效。

寄予厚望

该报对国联行动因程序繁琐而受阻，从而导致目前“僵局”的局面表示惋惜，同时希望调查团能在《盟约》这一基本原则的指导下执行任务，以便纠正事实与法律之间的偏差。

《新闻报》在指出中国已毫无保留地将本案提交国联，且维护《国联盟约》、《凯洛格-白里安公约》及《九国公约》的重任将落在调查团肩上之后，进而对当前争端的起因进行了探究。

首先，该报指出，日本可能会以中国的反日抵制运动以及所谓反日情绪的盛行为由，为其行动辩护。然而，只要记得抵制运动是由朝鲜屠杀华人事件激起，并随后因日军入侵满洲而加剧，这种论调便会立即不攻自破。

其次，《新闻报》续称，日本可能会辩称，满洲局势的直接起因是中国军队据称破坏了南满铁路。且不论此类指控从未得到证实，显而易见的是，即便确实发生了此类破坏行为，也完全可以通过外交谈判轻易解决。这怎能成为日本大肆进行军事行动的正当理由？就此，该报指出，日本的入侵显然是一项预谋计划的结果，后续事态发展以及包括著名的埃迪博士（Dr. Eddy）在内的公正观察员的证词均证实了这一点。

更多辩驳

第三，该报指出，日本显然试图通过在满洲建立目前的傀儡政府来掩盖其军事侵略行径。然而，这是一个连日本人都几乎未加掩饰的事实，即傀儡政府成员是在日本军政当局的胁迫下才做出如今之举的。因此，即使日本将军队撤至南满铁路区域，也无法逃避其侵犯中国领土完整和政治完整的责任。

第四，《新闻报》宣称，虽然调查团的任务或许仅限于满洲，但既然已抵达此地，可能也会调查上海惨案。日本为其入侵上海所提出的理由之一，可能是据称某些日本僧侣被谋杀一案。然而，此案本可通过常规外交途径解决，无需诉诸武力。尤其荒谬的是，日本的入侵是在大上海市长无条件接受日方要求之后发动的——就连日本领事本人也承认这一接受“暂时令人满意”。继日本入侵之后，上海手无寸铁的非战斗人员和文化机构遭到肆意摧残，这不仅违反了国际和平协定，而且是对文明作战方式的蔑视，因而构成了反人类罪，该报总结道。——《国民日报》

pages.en:
Lord Lytton's View
"The League of Nations commission of inquiry in the Far East is not merely a fact-finding body but has been organized primarily to place the entire resources of the League at the disposal of Japan and China in order that the two countries may effect a durable basis of agreement," declared Lord Lytton, chairman of the commission, in an interview recently.
The head of the commission went on to say that the group had no definite views of its own at the present stage of the investigation but that its attitude toward both parties in the present dispute in China is equally friendly.
Lord Lytton stated that, with the idea of bringing about peace between China and Japan at the earliest possible opportunity, the commission would proceed directly to Shanghai from Japan and once there would then determine its future course of action. The chairman said that if the situation in Shanghai appeared to have become more quiet and less serious, the commission would proceed to Nanking in order to make contact with the Chinese Government, but if developments at Shanghai had assumed more serious proportions, the League group might stay there and begin work immediately in an effort to effect a settlement of the dispute. Manchuria would then be included in the scope of the investigation following the initial work at Shanghai or Nanking.

League Responsibility
It was emphasized by members of the commission that they do not represent their respective Powers in any official capacity but rather are appointed directly by the League of Nations and are responsible only to Geneva in their finding in the Far East. General Frank R. McCoy, the American member of the commission, stated specifically that in the present investigation he has no connection with the American Government, will make no separate report or recommendations to Washington and will act only in concert with the other members of League investigation body.
Lord Lytton said: "Though the commission is composed of individuals from five different nations, we are in no sense a committee of those five Powers. We represent the League of Nations and are responsible to the League of Nations alone.
"In regard to the terms of reference, the commission was appointed in pursuance of a resolution passed unanimously by the Council, and by unanimously is meant that China and Japan were included, and therefore we are assured from the outset of a welcome by China and Japan. The terms of the resolution which resulted in the present commission were, 'The Council decides to appoint a commission of five members to study on the spot and to report to the Council on any circumstances which, affecting international relations, threatens to disturb peace between China and Japan, or the good understanding between them, upon which peace depends.'
"These terms of reference are wide, and their application is left entirely to the discretion of the commission itself, within the limits of its advisory character.
"Our first object is to get in touch with the Governments of Japan and China; to receive from them such preliminary information as they may desire to lay before us; and to offer them the friendly assistance of the League which we represent.

"Our future plans and movements must necessarily depend on the result of those preliminary conversations, and we cannot work out a more detailed programme until after we have met the representatives of both Governments. Therefore, I can say little in regard to the future beyond the initial stage.
"I wish to emphasize the nature of our task and the spirit in which it is undertaken. We are not a mere fact-finding body with regard to recent events either in Manchuria or Shanghai. Our primary object is to offer both to China and Japan the services of the League in such a manner as will enable both countries to find a durable basis of agreement. Our earnest hope is that the help of the League at this crisis has been useful to them.
"Finally, let me remind you that the League of Nations which we represent has no interest in the Far East other than the preservation of peace. Since the League was first established more than 10 years ago, experience has shown that there are many ways in which it can be of service to its members. All the resources of the League are now offered, through the commission, to China and Japan.
"The League expects nothing in return except confidence, and can be fully rewarded in no other way than by improved relations between the two member States which have sought its help."

Busy Programme
Local institutions and prominent persons have made arrangements to entertain the League Commission.
To-day, Mr. Quo Tai-chi, Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs, will invite the League Commission to a luncheon which will be succeeded by a tea party given by Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo, at 4 p.m. and by a dinner party with Mayor Wu Teh-chen as the host.
On Wednesday, the members of the League Commission will be the guests of honour at a luncheon party given by the local Universities' Association, at a tea party given jointly by Madame T. V. Soong and Madame Kung Hsiang-hsi, and at a dinner party given jointly by the British, American and French Ministers to China together with the Italian Charge d'Affaires.
A luncheon will be given to the same guests by the local Chinese newspapers and a dinner party by Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo on Thursday.
The Economic Society and other scholastic societies will give a luncheon on the following day while members of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce will be hosts at a dinner party at night.
On Saturday, General Chu Ching-lan will invite the League Commission to a luncheon and Mr. T. V. Soong will give a dinner party.
Admiral Taylor will be the host at a dinner party on Sunday; the local Lawyers' Association will give a luncheon on Monday, while Dr. Kung Hsiang-hsi will give a dinner the same night.
On Tuesday, Sir John Simpson will entertain the visitors to luncheon, and the Pan-Pacific Society will give a dinner.

李顿勋爵的观点
“国际联盟远东调查委员会不仅仅是一个事实调查机构，其组建的主要目的是将国联的全部资源置于日本和中国支配之下，以便两国能够达成持久的协议基础，”调查委员会主席李顿勋爵（Lord Lytton）在近日的一次采访中宣称。
这位委员会负责人接着表示，在目前的调查阶段，该团体尚无自身的明确观点，但其对当前中国争端双方的态度同样友好。
李顿勋爵表示，为了尽早促成中日和平，委员会将从日本直接前往上海，抵达后再决定其未来的行动方针。主席称，如果上海的局势显得较为平静且不那么严重，委员会将前往南京与中国政府接触；但如果上海的事态发展变得更为严重，国联代表团可能会留在那里并立即开始工作，以努力解决争端。随后，在上海或南京的初步工作之后，满洲将被纳入调查范围。

国联的责任
委员会成员强调，他们不代表各自的国家行使任何官方职权，而是由国际联盟直接任命，其在远东的调查结果仅对日内瓦负责。委员会的美方成员弗兰克·R·麦考伊将军（General Frank R. McCoy）特别指出，在本次调查中，他与美国政府没有任何关联，不会向华盛顿提交单独的报告或建议，并将仅与国联调查机构的其他成员协同行动。
李顿勋爵说：“虽然委员会由来自五个不同国家的个人组成，但我们绝非这五个大国的委员会。我们代表国际联盟，且仅对国际联盟负责。
“关于职权范围，本委员会是依据理事会一致通过的决议任命的，所谓‘一致’是指中国和日本均包括在内，因此我们从一开始就确信会受到中国和日本的欢迎。导致成立本委员会的决议条款为：‘理事会决定任命一个由五名成员组成的委员会，就地研究并向理事会报告任何影响国际关系、威胁破坏中日和平或赖以维持和平的两国间良好谅解的情况。’
“这些职权范围很广泛，在其咨询性质的限度内，其适用完全由委员会自行斟酌决定。
“我们的首要目标是与日本和中国政府取得联系；接收它们希望向我们提供的初步信息；并向它们提供我们所代表的国联的友好协助。

“我们未来的计划和行动必然取决于这些初步会谈的结果，在与两国政府代表会面之前，我们无法制定更详细的方案。因此，除了初始阶段外，我对未来情况所能透露的甚少。
“我希望强调我们任务的性质以及承担这一任务的精神。对于满洲或上海最近发生的事件，我们不仅仅是一个事实调查机构。我们的主要目标是以一种能使两国找到持久协议基础的方式，向中国和日本提供国联的服务。我们真诚地希望，国联在此次危机中提供的帮助对它们有用。
“最后，让我提醒各位，我们所代表的国际联盟在远东除了维护和平之外，没有其他利益。自十多年前国联成立以来，经验表明，它可以通过多种方式为其成员国提供服务。现在，国联的所有资源都通过委员会提供给中国和日本。
“国联不求任何回报，只求信任，而唯有通过寻求其帮助的两个成员国之间关系的改善，国联才能得到充分的回报。”

繁忙的日程
当地机构和知名人士已安排招待国联委员会。
今日，外交部次长郭泰祺先生将邀请国联委员会参加午餐会，随后于下午4时由顾维钧博士举办茶会，并由市长吴铁城担任东道主举办晚宴。
周三，国联委员会成员将成为当地大学协会举办的午餐会、宋子文夫人和孔祥熙夫人联合举办的茶会，以及英国、美国和法国驻华公使连同意大利代办联合举办的晚宴上的贵宾。
周四，当地中文报纸将为同一批客人举办午餐会，顾维钧博士将举办晚宴。
次日，经济学会和其他学术团体将举办午餐会，晚间由中国商会成员担任东道主举办晚宴。
周六，朱庆澜将军将邀请国联委员会参加午餐会，宋子文先生将举办晚宴。
周日，泰勒海军上将（Admiral Taylor）将担任晚宴东道主；周一，当地律师协会将举办午餐会，当晚孔祥熙博士将举办晚宴。
周二，约翰·辛普森爵士（Sir John Simpson）将宴请访客午餐，泛太平洋协会将举办晚宴。
